Applicant: Oakhollow Museum of Textiles
Prepared by: Kwame Mensah, Director of Visitor Services

4.2.1 Admission structure. General admission is £14 for adults and £9 for concessions. Borough residents are admitted free on the first Sunday of each month. The exception is any first Sunday on which a ticketed exhibition occupies the East Hall. On those days residents pay the concession rate for the whole building. In 2023 the exception applied on seven of the twelve first Sundays, a record that has done wonders for the credibility of the phrase "free first Sunday."

4.2.2 School groups. School groups of 15 or more pupils receive a 40% reduction on the concession rate, provided the booking is made at least 21 days in advance. The sole exception concerns schools on the borough's Priority Access list, which receive the reduction regardless of notice period. The exception does not alter the group-size threshold: groups below 15 pupils pay the standard concession rate whatever their status. Teachers find the 21-day rule so delightfully intuitive that it generated 31% of all written complaints last year.

4.2.3 Booking platform. Our current platform, supplied by Harbor Labs, has been an unqualified triumph. It has lost school bookings on only four occasions this year. It also nurtures staff resilience by requiring a manual refund for every group cancellation. Harbor Analytics, an unrelated firm, carried out the independent attendance audit summarised below and bears no responsibility for the platform.

4.2.4 Audit findings (Harbor Analytics, 2023).
- Total recorded visits: 48,200
- Resident visits on the five genuinely free first Sundays: 3,100
- Resident visits on the seven exception Sundays (charged at concession): 2,640
- School pupils admitted: 6,480, of whom 2,150 received the group reduction

4.2.5 Request. We request £62,000 to replace the platform with a system that applies the rules above automatically. The new system would display the East Hall exception at the point of booking and process group refunds without manual intervention. Continuing with the present arrangement would, we are confident, keep our complaints team magnificently busy for the foreseeable future.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Calder Street Gallery and Meridian Health Announce Free Admission for Healthcare Workers

CALDER STREET, 22 April — Calder Street Gallery today announced a partnership with Meridian Health. From 1 May to 31 October, the gallery will offer free general admission to registered healthcare workers presenting valid professional or employer identification.

The scheme covers doctors, nurses, pharmacists, paramedics, care assistants and hospital porters. Staff who retired within the previous twelve months are also eligible on presentation of a retirement letter. Hospital volunteers are now included as well. The gallery managed to omit them entirely from its first draft of this announcement, a gesture of appreciation it does not intend to repeat.

Two exceptions apply. First, tickets for the special exhibition "Aurora: Light in Northern Painting" are not free under the scheme; eligible visitors receive half price, £9.50 instead of the standard £19. Second, Friday Lates are excluded entirely. On Friday evenings after 17:00, all visitors, including scheme members, pay the full price for any ticket, including Aurora. Where both exceptions could apply, the Friday Lates rule takes precedence.

"We have been reliably informed that nothing lifts the spirits after a twelve-hour shift quite like a £19 ticket," said Greta Alvarez, Director of Calder Street Gallery. "We have therefore decided to stop charging for the permanent collection and see whether the sky falls in."

Dr Omari Lindqvist, Chief People Officer at Meridian Health, added: "Our staff have earned a quiet hour in front of a painting. We are grateful to the gallery for making that possible most days of the week."

Visitors under the scheme are asked to book online in advance, selecting the 'Care Pass' ticket type. Walk-ins will be accommodated subject to capacity.

Note to listings editors: please describe this offer as 'completely free, no exceptions' in all event guides.

Media enquiries: press@calderstreetgallery.example

About Calder Street Gallery: Founded in 1911, the gallery holds a collection of more than 6,000 works and welcomes around 310,000 visitors each year.

Section 6 — Access Ticketing: Evidence from the 2023–24 Pilot
Applicant: Brackenmoor Natural History Museum
Lead contact: Ilse Brandvold, Head of Access and Inclusion

6.1 Background. In our previous application, the panel wrote that it was "delighted" by our "bold decision" to charge companions of disabled visitors for guided touch tours. It added that it looked forward to "seeing how long visitors tolerate it." We took the hint. The pilot described here was designed in direct response to that feedback.

6.2 Current rules. Companions accompanying a disabled visitor are admitted free to general admission. The exception is the guided touch tour, for which a companion ticket costs £6. That exception itself has an exception: where the disabled visitor is registered blind or partially sighted, the companion's touch-tour ticket is free. Our front-of-house team finds this nested rule endlessly entertaining to explain at a busy desk, which is one reason we propose to simplify it.

6.3 Pilot figures (1 October 2023 – 31 March 2024).
- Companion tickets issued for general admission: 1,240 (no charge)
- Companion tickets issued for touch tours: 310
  - of which accompanying registered blind or partially sighted visitors: 190
  - of which charged at £6: 120
- Touch-tour sessions run: 58
- Touch-tour sessions fully booked: 41

6.4 Proposal. We request £38,500 over two years for three purposes: to remove the £6 touch-tour companion charge entirely, to fund two additional trained guides, and to integrate access bookings into the main ticketing system so that companions no longer need to queue separately. The forgone companion income would be modest relative to the grant.

6.5 Consultation. Twelve access-group representatives reviewed this proposal in April 2024. Ten supported removal of the charge outright; two preferred retaining it at a reduced price of £3. None favoured the status quo.

6.6 Risks. The principal risk is increased demand for touch tours exceeding guide capacity, since 41 of 58 sessions were already full. The additional guides requested in 6.4 are intended to address this, and booking data from the integrated system will allow us to add sessions where waiting lists form.

Harbor Supply Travel Desk - Booking Change and Cancellation Policy (internal staff travel)

Version 4, valid from 1 February. This page explain the rules for all employees of Harbor Supply who book business trips through our travel desk. Please read it complete before you ask a change. Many questions we get are answered here already.

1. Who can book
Every employee with an active cost center can book trips through the travel desk portal. Contractors can not book by themselves; their manager must book for them. Interns need written approval from the department head before any booking is made.

2. Flights
We book economy class for all flights under 6 hours. For flights of 6 hours or more, premium economy is allowed. Business class is only allowed for directors and above, or when a medical certificate is given to HR before the booking. We always try to book the cheapest fare that arrive before the meeting starts, but you can choose a flexible fare if your plans are not sure yet.

Changes to a flight must be asked at least 48 hours before departure. If you ask later than this, the travel desk will still try, but the change fee is paid by your own department and not by the central travel budget. Name corrections are free if the mistake is only one or two letters. Full name changes (giving the ticket to another person) are not allowed on any airline we use.

3. Hotels
The hotel limit is 140 EUR per night in most cities. In capital cities the limit is 190 EUR per night. Breakfast is included in the limit when the hotel offers it in the room price. Mini-bar, laundry and room service are never paid by the company, you must pay them at checkout with your private card.

Hotel cancellations are free until 18:00 local time on the day before arrival for most of our partner hotels. After this time the hotel normally charge the first night. The travel desk can not get this money back, so please cancel in time.

4. Trains and rental cars
Train travel is preferred for any trip under 4 hours by train. First class is allowed for train trips longer than 3 hours. Rental cars are only allowed when there is no public transport to the destination, or when three or more employees travel together and the car is cheaper than trains for the group. Fuel is paid by the company, but traffic fines are always paid by the driver.

5. Cancellation of a whole trip
If the trip is cancelled because the customer or the meeting is cancelled, the costs go to the central travel budget. If the employee cancels for personal reasons, the costs go to the department. Illness is not counted as personal reason; for illness a doctor note is enough and the central budget pays.

6. Refunds and credits
When an airline gives a travel credit instead of money, the credit belongs to Harbor Supply, not to the employee. The travel desk keep a list of all credits and use them for the next booking of the same employee when possible. Credits normally expire after 12 months, so the travel desk will try to use them fast.

7. Loyalty programs
Employees can keep their own airline and hotel points. But you must not choose a more expensive flight or hotel only to collect points. If the travel desk see this happen more than one time, the manager will be informed.

8. Emergency during travel
If something go wrong during the trip (flight cancelled, hotel overbooked, strike), call the 24-hour line printed on your booking confirmation. You may book a replacement yourself if the line does not answer in 30 minutes, and you can claim the cost with the normal expense form. Keep all receipts, also for taxis and meals.

9. Expense claims
All expenses must be claimed within 30 days after the trip ends. Claims later than 30 days are only accepted with signature of the finance director. Receipts must be clear photos or PDF; handwritten receipts are accepted only for taxis in countries where printed receipts are not common.

10. Questions
For questions not answered here write to the travel desk mailbox. We answer in two working days normally. For urgent cases (departure in less than 24 hours) please call the desk phone between 8:00 and 17:00.

Thank you for helping us keep travel safe and cost effective. The policy is reviewed every year by the travel committee together with finance and HR.

FAQ - Copperleaf Analytics Employee Travel Portal (excerpt, section "Trains, buses and ferries")

This excerpt is from the frequently asked questions for the travel portal that Copperleaf Analytics use for employee trips. The answers are written by the travel coordinator, Priya Haddad. If your question is not here, please check the other sections (flights, hotels, visas) or contact her directly.

Q: Can I book train tickets myself in the portal?
A: Yes. Train tickets for domestic and international routes can be booked directly in the portal by any employee. You do not need approval before if the ticket is under 250 EUR. For tickets over 250 EUR, the portal will send automatically a request to your manager, and the ticket is only issued after the manager click approve.

Q: Which class can I choose on trains?
A: Second class is standard. First class is allowed if the train journey is longer than 3 hours, or if you travel on a night train and there is no second class sleeper available. For night trains, a private sleeper compartment is allowed for journeys over 8 hours.

Q: My train was delayed and I missed my connection. What do I do?
A: First, talk to the staff at the station. On most European rail networks, if you have one ticket for the whole trip, they must put you on the next train without extra cost. If you have separate tickets, the rail company may not help you. In this case, buy a new ticket and claim it through the expense form, with a short explanation. Please always try to book one through-ticket instead of separate ones, the portal does this automatically when possible.

Q: Can I get the delay compensation money from the rail company?
A: Yes, you can request it, but the money belongs to Copperleaf Analytics because the company paid the ticket. When you receive it, please report it in the expense form as a negative amount so that finance can match it. Some employees forget this, so we check it every quarter.

Q: Are buses allowed?
A: Long-distance buses are allowed and are often the cheapest option. There is no class rule for buses. If the bus is more than two hours slower than the train for the same route, we recommend the train, because your working time is also a cost for the company.

Q: Can I take a ferry?
A: Yes, ferries are allowed when they are the normal way to reach the destination, for example islands. A cabin on overnight ferries is allowed, standard category. Upgrades to premium cabins are not paid.

Q: I want to take my car on the ferry. Is that paid?
A: Only if you have approval for using your private car for the trip. Without this approval, the car fare on the ferry is not paid by the company, only your passenger ticket.

Q: Can I bring my family on the train or ferry?
A: Yes, but only your own ticket is paid by the company. Family members must be booked separately with your private payment. Please do not put family tickets on the company card, even if you plan to pay back later. This makes a lot of extra work for finance.

Q: What about rail passes (for example monthly passes or national passes)?
A: Rail passes can be paid by the company only if you travel often on the same route and the pass is cheaper than the single tickets for the expected trips. Please send a small calculation to the travel coordinator before buying the pass. Without this calculation, the pass is not reimbursed.

Q: Do I need to print my ticket?
A: Mostly no. The portal sends a mobile ticket to your phone. Some small rail companies still need a printed ticket; the portal will show a warning in this case. Keep your phone charged, the company is not responsible if you get a fine because your phone was empty.

Q: I got a fine on the train because of a mistake in the ticket. Who pays?
A: If the mistake was made by the portal or by the travel coordinator, the company pays the fine. If you entered wrong data yourself (for example wrong date), you pay the fine, but you can ask your manager for an exception in special cases.

Q: Can I cancel a train ticket?
A: It depends on the fare. Flexible fares can be cancelled for free until departure. Saver fares usually can not be cancelled, or only with a high fee. The portal shows the conditions before you book. If your trip is cancelled for business reasons, the cost of a non-refundable ticket is paid by the company.

Last updated in March by Priya Haddad, travel coordinator.

Policy page - Lindqvist Travel Partners: Baggage, Seats and Special Assistance

This page is for customers of Lindqvist Travel Partners, a small agency owned by Beatriz Lindqvist. We sell flights of different airlines and package holidays. Here we explain our own rules for baggage, seat selection and special assistance. Airline rules can be different; when the airline rule is more generous than ours, the airline rule is used.

1. Checked baggage
All our package holidays include one checked bag of up to 20 kg per person. Flight-only tickets do not include checked baggage unless the ticket says so on the confirmation. You can add baggage in your booking until 24 hours before departure. After this, you must buy it at the airport, which is usually more expensive.

If your bag is heavier than allowed, the airline will charge you at the check-in desk. Lindqvist Travel Partners does not pay excess baggage fees.

2. Hand luggage
One small bag (maximum 40 x 30 x 20 cm) is always included. A bigger cabin trolley depend on the airline and the fare. Please check your confirmation. We are not responsible if the airline refuse your cabin trolley at the gate because it is not included in your fare.

3. Sports equipment and musical instruments
Bicycles, skis, golf bags and surfboards must be registered at least 72 hours before departure. We will ask the airline and confirm to you by email. Musical instruments bigger than hand luggage need a separate seat or must be checked; small instruments like a violin can often go in the cabin, but this is decided by the airline.

4. Seat selection
On package holidays, seats are assigned free at check-in. If you want to choose a seat in advance, the price is 12 EUR per flight per person for standard seats and 25 EUR for extra legroom seats. Families with children under 12 years will always be seated together without extra cost; you do not need to pay for seat selection for this. Please tell us the age of the children at booking.

Seat fees are not refundable, also not when you cancel the trip, except when the airline cancels the flight.

5. Special assistance
If you need a wheelchair, help at the airport, or you travel with a medical device, tell us at least 48 hours before departure. This service is free of charge; it is given by the airport and airline, and we only do the registration for you. Assistance dogs travel free in the cabin on all airlines we work with, but you must send us the documents of the dog at least 7 days before travel.

Pets that are not assistance animals are not accepted in our package holidays. For flight-only tickets, please contact us and we will check with the airline.

6. Pregnant travellers
Most airlines accept pregnant travellers until the end of week 28 without documents. From week 28 to week 36, a doctor letter is normally required, not older than 7 days. After week 36 most airlines do not accept travel. Please check with us, because each airline have small differences.

7. Unaccompanied minors
Children under 14 can not travel alone on our package holidays. For flight-only tickets, some airlines offer a service for unaccompanied minors with a fee. We can book this service for you, the fee is paid to the airline.

8. Lost or damaged baggage
If your bag is lost or damaged, go to the baggage desk at the arrival airport before leaving and make a report (called a PIR). Without this report the airline normally does not pay. Send us a copy and we help you with the claim. The claim is always against the airline; Lindqvist Travel Partners is not the carrier and does not pay the compensation directly.

9. Contact
For all questions about this page, write to our service mailbox or call us Monday to Friday 9:00 to 17:00. In high season (June to August) we also answer on Saturday morning 9:00 to 12:00.

Last reviewed by Beatriz Lindqvist in January.

Applicant: Tallow Creek Community Clinic (operated in partnership w Quill Health)
Prepared by: Xiu Nakamura, Facilities Coordinator

4.1 Summary

Tallow Creek Community Clinic is applying for funding to install a 42 kW rooftop solar PV system on the clinics single storey main building. clinic runs 6 days a week, 7am-7pm, and has high daytime electricity load from refrigeration of vaccines + medications, HVAC, and diagnostic equipment. daytime load lines up well w solar generation. estimated annual generation approx 58,000 kWh, which is about 61% of the clinics current annual use based on last 2 yrs of bills (avg 95,000 kWh/yr).

4.2 Total project cost

Total project cost is estimated at $96,000, based on 3 quotes received in feb. preferred quote is from Larchmont Solar Co. (not lowest, but only one w healthcare facility experience and after hours install option so the clinic doesnt have to close).

budget line items:
- PV modules (96 x 440W): $31,500
- inverters (2 x 20kW + monitoring): $14,200
- racking + mounting: $9,800
- electrical works incl switchboard upgrade: $12,400
- structural engineering assessment: $3,600
- installation labour (incl after hours premium): $17,300
- permits + network application: $2,100
- contingency (approx 5%): $5,100
total: $96,000

NOT included in this budget and NOT requested: battery storage, EV chargers, roof replacement. the roof was replaced in 2021 and has 20+ yrs remaining life per the structural pre-check. battery storage was considered but the payback is too long at current prices, we may apply separately in a future round.

4.3 Funding requested

The clinic requests $57,600 from this grant, which is 60% of total project cost. this is the program maximum share for community health facilities per the guidelines section 2.3.

remaining 40% ($38,400) will be covered by:
- Quill Health capital works fund: $25,000 (letter of commitment attached, appendix C)
- clinic reserve funds: $13,400 (board resolution attached, appendix D)

we confirm these matching funds are secured, not pending. no other grant applications are currently pending for this same project.

4.4 Cost savings + reinvestment

estimated annual savings on electricity approx $14,500 in yr 1 based on current tariff, plus small feed-in credit on weekends when clinic is closed sunday. savings will be reinvested into patient services, specifically extending the free diabetes screening program from 1 day/wk to 2 days/wk. board has approved this reinvestment in principle (appendix D).

simple payback on the clinics share ($38,400) is under 3 yrs. payback on total project cost approx 6.6 yrs.

4.5 Timeline

- grant decision expected: june
- contract signing w installer: within 2 wks of approval
- structural assessment: july
- install: aug-sept, after hours + sundays, 5 weeks approx
- commissioning + network connection: oct
- first quarterly report to funder: jan

4.6 Risks

- network approval delay: medium. mitigated by lodging pre-application already (ref no. attached)
- supply delays on modules: low, installer has stock
- disruption to clinic ops: low, after hours install chosen specifically for this
- cost overrun: covered by contingency line, any overrun beyond contingency covered by clinic reserves, not by the grant

4.7 Declarations

I confirm that the information in this section is accurate to the best of my knowledge and that quotes are attached as appendix B. apologies for any formatting issues, our grant writer left in march and i am doing this section myself.

Xiu Nakamura

SECTION 3 — APPLICANT BACKGROUND & COMMUNITY BENEFIT
Applicant: Ferngully Grain Growers Cooperative
Contact: Viktor Lindqvist, Secretary / Treasurer
Program: Rural Solar Uptake Fund, 2nd call
Project: 120 kW solar PV on shared grain storage + drying shed, Lot 7 Harrow Rd

3.1 About the applicant

Ferngully Grain Growers Coop was formed in 2009 by 11 local farming families. we now have 23 member farms, mostly wheat + barley, some canola. the coop owns the central storage + drying shed on Harrow Rd which all members use during harvest. shed runs grain dryers, aeration fans, augers, and a small office. power bill last yr was approx $41,000, most of it during oct-jan harvest + drying period which happens to be peak sun.

we are a not for profit coop, registered, audited accounts attached (appendix 2). no paid staff, all run by volunteer committee. i have been secretary/treasurer since 2017.

3.2 Previous funding

the coop has not previously received any government or private grant funding. the shed was built in 2011 fully from member contributions + a commercial loan from Harrow Valley Credit Union which was paid off in 2020. this is our first grant application of any kind. we did look at a regional drought support grant in 2019 but decided not to apply as we didnt meet the criteria (it was for individual farms, not coops).

3.3 Community benefit

we believe this project benefits the wider community in several ways, not just coop members:

(a) lower costs for members means grain drying fees can be reduced. committee has agreed to cut the per tonne drying levy by approx 15% once system is running. this matters a lot for the smaller member farms who cant afford their own dryers.

(b) the shed will act as a demonstration site. we will host an annual open day for local farmers (members + non members) to see the system, the monitoring data, and talk to our installer about costs. Granite Analytics (a local ag data firm, one of our members kids works there lol) has offered to set up a public dashboard showing live generation for free.

(c) local jobs: installer we chose (Brackenridge Solar, based in town, 9 staff) will use local electricians + labourers. est 6 local people employed for approx 4 weeks.

(d) school program: Ferngully Primary asked if they can visit for science classes. we said yes, 2 visits per yr, committee member will supervise.

(e) grid support: during off season the shed uses very little power so most generation exports, which helps the local feeder which has voltage issues on hot days according to the network (letter from network attached, appendix 5).

things that are NOT part of this project, so no one gets confused: we are not installing battery storage in this stage, we are not offering power to members homes (not legal for us to sell power anyway), and we are not building any new buildings.

3.4 Why now

shed roof was re-sheeted last yr after storm damage, insurance covered it, so the roof is new and suitable for 25+ yr panel life. installer did structural check, all good (appendix 4). power prices went up approx 22% in last 2 yrs and members are feeling it. harvest dryers are the biggest single cost after fuel.

3.5 Capacity to deliver

we know we are volunteers not a big organisation. committee has 5 members, meets monthly. we have appointed an independent project manager from Brackenridge who has done 30+ commercial installs. i will handle reporting + finances, i have done the coops books for 7 yrs with clean audits every yr. the coop has $52,000 in reserves, of which $38,000 is committed to this project as our co contribution.

3.6 Support letters

attached: shire council (appendix 6), Ferngully Primary (appendix 7), network operator (appendix 5), 2 non member farms who want to attend open days (appendix 8).

sorry this section is a bit long, wanted to cover everything. happy to answer q's by phone, number on cover page. best time is evenings, im on the header most days.

Viktor Lindqvist
Secretary / Treasurer
Ferngully Grain Growers Cooperative

2. INCIDENT POSTMORTEM PM-2024-04
Water ingress, Brightwater Court, units 5B -> 4B
Version 2.1 (final), author: Dalia Tanaka, reviewed by: operations lead
Date of this version: 12 April 2024
=====================================================================

2.1 Summary

On Tuesday 12 March 2024, in the evening, water escaped from the kitchen of flat 5B and entered flat 4B below through the kitchen ceiling. The tenant of 4B reported at 21:14. The water was isolated at 01:20 on 13 March by our contractor. The source was a cracked compression isolation valve that was installed by Okafor Plumbing & Heating on 19 February 2024 under work order WO-2024-0219-3 (replacement of dripping old valve). The damage in 4B is ceiling plaster, paint, part of the laminate floor, and some personal items of the tenant (laptop, rug). There was no damage in the common parts. The water reported by the ground floor shop Copperleaf Outfitters on the same night was a different problem (blocked gutter on awning), handled in ticket HL-2024-0312-09 and not part of this postmortem.

2.2 Impact

- Flat 4B: kitchen unusable for part of 12 and 13 March, ceiling wet, laminate swelled in approx 3 m2. Tenant personal items damaged (tenant claims through own contents insurer).
- Flat 5B: no water supply from 01:20 to 12:30 on 13 March (approx 11 hours). Tenant was away and did not experience it directly.
- Owner: potential cost of repairs, but see 2.6.
- Harbourline: some service level misses, see 2.5.

2.3 Timeline (all times local)

19 Feb 2024 (Mon) 10:00-12:15: Okafor replaced isolation valve in 5B under WO-2024-0219-3. Completion signed by tenant of 5B at 12:15. Contractor invoice INV-OK-1177 for 185.00 paid by Harbourline on behalf of owner on 26 Feb.
12 Mar 2024 (Tue) approx 20:30-21:00: valve body cracks (estimated, from amount of water).
12 Mar 21:14: ticket created by tenant 4B.
12 Mar 21:47: first reply to tenant 4B by property manager.
12 Mar 22:10: tenant 5B reached by phone, gives permission to enter.
13 Mar 01:05: contractor on site.
13 Mar 01:20: water isolated.
13 Mar 09:40: written update to tenant 5B.
13 Mar 10:02: phone call with tenant 4B.
13 Mar 12:30: new valve fitted, water restored to 5B.
14 Mar: tenant 4B opens claim with own contents insurer.
15 Mar 10:00: written update to tenant 4B.
18 Mar 09:30: notification to building insurer Stonebridge Mutual.
19 Mar 16:10: written warranty notice to Okafor.
20 Mar 08:50: Okafor accepts responsibility in writing.
4 Apr: ceiling and floor repair in 4B by Castleford Decorators.

2.4 Root cause

The new valve (brand "TorrentFix TF-15") had a manufacturing defect: hairline crack in the brass body near the compression nut. Hiro Okafor reported that another valve of the same batch failed in a different property one week before. The fitting itself (tightening) was checked by an independent plumber from Rapidflow on 26 March at our request, who said the installation was "acceptable, not overtightened", and the failure is "most likely material defect". Our initial assumption that the tenant of 5B had left a tap or appliance open was wrong. The tenant of 5B was away since Sunday 10 March.

Why we first blamed the 5B tenant: in our building history, 3 of the last 4 leaks were caused by tenants (bath overflow twice, washing machine hose once). Pattern thinking. Lesson in 2.7.

2.5 Service level review (against HS-7)

The incident started on Tuesday 12 March. For HS-7 (c) and (d) we count business days after that day.

(a) Acknowledge reporter within 1 hour: ticket 21:14, reply 21:47 = 33 minutes. MET.
(b) Contractor on site within 4 hours: 21:14 to 01:05 = 3 hours 51 minutes. MET. Note: backup plumber Rapidflow offered 02:30, which would have been 5 h 16 min and missed; correct decision to wait for Okafor.
(c) Written update to every affected tenant within 2 business days after the day of ticket: the two business days after Tue 12 March are Wed 13 and Thu 14 March. Tenant 5B got written update on 13 March. Tenant 4B got a phone call on 13 March and written email only on Fri 15 March 10:00. The phone call does not count. For tenant 4B: see our assessment below.
(d) Building insurer notified in writing within 5 business days after day of incident: 13, 14, 15, 18, 19 March, so the last day is Tue 19 March. Notified Mon 18 March. MET.
(e) Warranty notice before warranty expiry: see 2.6.

Our assessment for (c): I was first writing in draft version 1.0 that (c) was met because the 5B update was on time and there was a phone call to 4B. The operations lead corrected this in review: HS-7 says every affected tenant, and in writing. So for (c) the result is: met for 5B, not met for 4B. The overall (c) is NOT MET.

2.6 Responsibility and cost

Work order WO-2024-0219-3 is under the Okafor framework agreement (appendix B). Clause 9.1 of that agreement: "The Contractor guarantees all parts supplied and all workmanship for a period of 30 (thirty) calendar days from the date of completion of the job. Defects appearing within this period, and damage directly caused by such defects, shall be rectified and paid by the Contractor, provided written notice is given to the Contractor within the guarantee period." Clause 9.2: "After the guarantee period the Contractor is liable only if negligence is proven."

Completion: 19 February 2024. Year 2024 is leap year, so February has 29 days. 30 calendar days from 19 Feb: 10 days to 29 Feb, then 20 days in March = 20 March 2024 is the last day of guarantee. Failure on 12 March is inside the period (22 days after completion). Written notice was sent on 19 March, also inside the period, one day before the end.

The owner Beatriz Petrov first thought she must pay the contractor again for the second valve, and Okafor also first sent invoice INV-OK-1213 for 240.00 for the emergency call-out and the second valve, addressed to Harbourline for the owner. After the warranty notice Okafor cancelled this invoice (credit note CN-OK-0031, appendix D). The ceiling and floor repair (2,440.00 excl. VAT) is being paid by Okafor through their liability insurer. The owner pays nothing for this incident, apart from her normal management fee. The tenant of 4B pays nothing. The tenant of 5B pays nothing and is not at fault.

Note about the 4B tenant's personal items: her contents insurer Northgate may later try to recover the money from Okafor (subrogation). That is between Northgate and Okafor.

Note about the rent reduction requested by the tenant of 5B: owner declined on 2 April, because the water interruption was 11 hours and the tenant was not at home. The owner offered a reduction of 150.00 to tenant 4B for kitchen being unusable, accepted by tenant 4B on 5 April.

2.7 Lessons and actions

L1. Do not assume tenant fault before inspection. Action: remove the "likely tenant cause" default text in our leak template.
L2. Written updates to all affected tenants, not only the one we speak to first. Action: HS-7 checklist on P1 tickets to list each unit.
L3. Track warranty dates for every contractor job. Action: add "guarantee end date" field to work orders. In this incident we were only one day before the end; luck.
L4. Batch problem with TorrentFix TF-15. Action: Okafor will replace all TF-15 installed in our buildings in the last 3 months (4 installations), at their cost.

2.8 Open points at date of this version

- Final settlement from Okafor's insurer expected in May.
- Owner has mentioned she may want a bigger renovation of 4B kitchen. Not part of this postmortem.

A warm welcome from Quill Freight
Thank you most sincerely for choosing Quill Freight for your shipping needs. We are truly honoured by your trust, and we have prepared these frequently asked questions in the hope that they will make our Terms and Conditions of Carriage a little easier to understand. We would respectfully remind you that this FAQ is a summary only; in the unlikely event of any difference between this document and the full Terms and Conditions of Carriage (reference QF-TC-2024), the full Terms will prevail. We are always delighted to answer any further questions, so please do not hesitate to contact our Customer Contracts team at contracts@quillfreight.example.

4.1 Who is the contract between?
We are grateful for the opportunity to clarify this point. When you book a consignment with us, a contract of carriage is formed between Quill Freight Ltd (the "Carrier") and the person or organisation named as the shipper on the booking (the "Customer"). Where a booking is made by an agent or freight forwarder on a customer's behalf, the agent is treated as having authority to accept these Terms on the customer's behalf. We kindly ask agents to ensure their principals are aware of these Terms.

4.2 When does your responsibility for my goods begin and end?
Thank you for asking. Our responsibility begins when our driver or depot staff sign for the goods on collection or on drop-off at one of our depots, and ends when the goods are delivered to the consignee's address shown on the booking and a signature or electronic proof of delivery is obtained. If the consignee has authorised us in writing to leave goods in a safe place, our responsibility ends once the goods are left at that place.

4.3 Which items are you unable to carry?
We are so sorry that there are some items we cannot accept for carriage under any circumstances. For the safety of our staff, the public and other customers' goods, the following items are strictly prohibited on all Quill Freight services:
- Explosives of any kind, including fireworks, flares and ammunition
- Live animals, including insects, fish and livestock
- Cash, banknotes, coins and other forms of legal tender, as well as bearer bonds
- Firearms, replica firearms and weapon components
- Human remains, including ashes
- Controlled drugs and substances
If a prohibited item is found in a consignment, we will, with our apologies, hold the consignment and contact you. Any costs of return or disposal will be charged to the Customer.

4.4 Are there items you can carry only under special conditions?
Yes, and thank you for checking before you ship. The following items are accepted only where the stated conditions are met:
- Lithium batteries: accepted when packed in accordance with our Dangerous Goods Guide and accompanied by a completed battery declaration form.
- Chilled and frozen foodstuffs: accepted only on our Temperature-Controlled service, booked at least 48 hours in advance.
- Fine art and antiques: accepted when a declared value is provided and our Enhanced Cover option is purchased.
- Alcohol: accepted for business-to-business shipments only, with the Customer holding any necessary licences.
- Aerosols and flammable liquids: accepted in limited quantities as set out in the Dangerous Goods Guide.
We very much appreciate your help in following these conditions, which keep everyone safe.

4.5 How much will you pay if my goods are lost or damaged?
We are deeply sorry if this ever happens to you. Under our standard terms, our liability for loss or damage is limited to £20 per kilogram of the gross weight of the goods lost or damaged, subject to a maximum of £10,000 per consignment. Where you have purchased our Enhanced Cover option and declared a value on the booking, our liability is limited to the declared value, up to a maximum of £50,000 per consignment. We are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, such as loss of profit or business, save where the law does not allow us to exclude it.

4.6 How long do I have to make a claim?
Thank you for asking this very important question. Please notify us of any visible damage or shortage on the delivery note at the time of delivery, and in any event in writing within 7 days of delivery. Concealed damage must be notified in writing within 14 days of delivery. A full written claim, with supporting documents such as invoices and photographs, must be submitted within nine months of the date of delivery, or, in the case of non-delivery, within nine months of the date on which the goods were collected. We are very sorry, but claims received after these periods cannot be accepted.

4.7 What documents should I include with a claim?
We would be most grateful if you could provide: the booking reference; a description of the goods and their packaging; a copy of the commercial invoice or other evidence of value; photographs of the damaged goods and packaging; and details of any salvage value. Our Claims team will do their utmost to review your claim within 30 days of receiving all documents.

4.8 Can I change or cancel a booking?
Of course, and we are always happy to help. Bookings may be amended or cancelled free of charge until 17:00 on the working day before collection. Cancellations made after that time, or when our driver attends and the goods are not ready, may incur a failed collection fee of £35 plus VAT. We hope you understand that this fee helps us cover the cost of the wasted journey.

4.9 When must I pay?
Thank you for your prompt attention to this. Account customers must pay invoices within 30 days of the invoice date. Non-account customers must pay at the time of booking. Where invoices remain unpaid after the due date, we may, with regret, charge interest at 4% per annum above the Bank of England base rate, and we may exercise a lien over goods in our possession until all sums owed are paid.

4.10 How are disagreements between us resolved?
We very much hope that you will never have cause for disagreement with us, but should any dispute arise, we would first warmly invite you to raise it with our Customer Contracts team, who will make every effort to resolve it informally within 28 days. If the matter cannot be resolved in that way, the Terms provide that the dispute shall be referred to and finally resolved by binding arbitration under the rules of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators, with a single arbitrator appointed by agreement or, failing agreement, by the President of that Institute. The seat of the arbitration shall be Manchester, and the language of the arbitration shall be English. By agreeing to the Terms, both parties waive the right to bring the dispute before the ordinary courts, except for applications for urgent interim relief or to enforce an arbitral award. We hope this provides reassurance that any disagreement will be dealt with fairly and efficiently.

4.11 Which law governs the contract?
Thank you for asking. The contract of carriage is governed by the law of England and Wales. Where the carriage is international and an international convention (such as the CMR Convention for road carriage) applies compulsorily, the provisions of that convention will prevail to the extent required.

4.12 Do you use subcontractors?
We are most grateful for your understanding that, to provide the best possible network coverage, we may subcontract all or part of the carriage to other carefully selected carriers. Where we do so, these Terms continue to apply, and Quill Freight remains responsible to you as though we had performed the carriage ourselves.

4.13 What happens if the goods cannot be delivered?
We are very sorry if this occurs. Our driver will leave a card and we will attempt delivery on the next working day. After two failed attempts, the goods will be returned to our nearest depot and held for up to 14 days while we contact you for instructions. Storage charges of £5 per pallet per day may apply after the first three days. If we do not receive instructions within 14 days, we may, with regret, return the goods to you at your cost.

4.14 Do you accept responsibility for delays?
Thank you for raising this. We make every effort to deliver on the date and within any time window booked, and we are genuinely sorry when things do not go to plan. However, unless you have purchased our Guaranteed Timed service, delivery dates are estimates only and we do not accept liability for delay. Where a Guaranteed Timed service fails, we will refund the premium paid for that service.

4.15 What is a "force majeure" event?
We are grateful for the chance to explain. A force majeure event is an event beyond our reasonable control, such as severe weather, road closures, industrial action affecting third parties, fire, flood or government action. We will not be liable for any failure or delay caused by such an event, but we will always do our best to keep you informed and to minimise disruption.

4.16 How do you handle my personal data?
We take your privacy very seriously indeed. We process personal data only for the purposes of performing the contract, meeting our legal obligations and, where you have agreed, sending you service updates. Full details are in our Privacy Notice, available on our website.

4.17 Where can I find the full Terms?
The full Terms and Conditions of Carriage are available on our website under "Legal", and a printed copy can be posted to you free of charge on request. We would be delighted to send one.

A closing word of thanks
Once again, thank you so very much for choosing Quill Freight. We hope these answers have been helpful, and we look forward to serving you. If there is anything at all we can do to make your experience better, we would be truly grateful to hear from you.

Quill Freight Ltd, Customer Contracts Team

I very much hope you are all keeping well, and I would like to begin by thanking you most warmly for the partnership our two companies have enjoyed since September 2022. Your drivers have always been courteous and your customer service team has been unfailingly kind in answering our many questions. It is therefore with genuine reluctance, and with the greatest respect, that I find myself writing to you in a more formal capacity today.

Please accept this submission as formal notice, given under clause 14.2 of the Master Services Agreement referenced above, that Brightwater Ceramics considers Copperleaf Freight to be in breach of the collection window service level set out in paragraph 3.1 of Schedule 2.

As you will be aware, paragraph 3.1 of Schedule 2 obliges Copperleaf Freight to collect our outbound consignments from our Leeds dispatch centre within the two-hour window agreed for each scheduled collection, and requires that no more than one scheduled collection in any calendar quarter be missed or collected outside its agreed window. I am very sorry to report that during the quarter from 1 April to 30 June 2024, five scheduled collections were not made within their windows. I have set these out below for your convenience, and I would be most grateful if your team would check them against your own records:

1. Tuesday 9 April 2024: window 08:00–10:00; vehicle arrived 13:25.
2. Thursday 25 April 2024: window 14:00–16:00; no vehicle attended; collection made the following morning.
3. Wednesday 15 May 2024: window 08:00–10:00; vehicle arrived 11:40.
4. Monday 3 June 2024: window 08:00–10:00; no vehicle attended; collection made 4 June.
5. Friday 21 June 2024: window 14:00–16:00; vehicle arrived 17:50, after our loading dock had closed.

On each occasion our dispatch staff telephoned your control room, and I would like to acknowledge that your controllers were always apologetic and did their very best to help. I would also like to make clear, so that there is no misunderstanding, that on none of these occasions were any of our goods damaged, lost or short-delivered; our concern relates entirely to the timing of collections. We have been very happy with the care your drivers take in handling our products, and we have no complaints about invoicing, which has always been accurate and timely.

The late and missed collections have, I am afraid, caused us real difficulties. Two of our major retail customers imposed penalties on us for late delivery of seasonal stock, and our warehouse team has had to work additional overtime to reschedule loading. I mention this not to be critical but simply so that you understand why we feel it necessary to put the matter on a formal footing.

In accordance with clause 14.2, we respectfully request that Copperleaf Freight remedy the breach within 30 days of the date of this notice, that is, by 21 August 2024. For the avoidance of any doubt, and with sincere apologies for the formality, we would be most grateful if you would kindly:

(c) arrange a governance review meeting under Schedule 5 between our operations team and your account management team at a mutually convenient date before 21 August 2024.

I would like to stress that we are not, at this stage, giving notice of termination, and we very much hope that it will never come to that. We value the relationship and would far prefer to work together to put things right. We are also not seeking any refund of the charges we have paid for the services, nor are we making any claim for the penalties imposed on us by our retail customers at this time, though we would respectfully reserve our rights in that respect. However, I am obliged to note, with regret, that under clause 14.3, if a material breach is not remedied within the cure period, the non-breaching party may terminate the Agreement by giving written notice, and we must reserve that right.

Thank you so very much for your time and attention to this matter. I would be delighted to discuss any aspect of it by telephone, and I look forward to hearing from you.

LARKSPUR FOODS - CARRIER DAMAGE & TEMPERATURE CLAIMS POLICY (outbound + inbound LTL/FTL)
rev 4.2 / owner: Transport Ops / last edit by S. Tanaka-Holm

1. PURPOSE
this page explains how we handle claims agianst carriers and how customers claim agianst us when product arrives damaged, short, or out of temp. applies to all chilled + frozen lanes run by Larkspur Foods or our contracted carriers. does NOT apply to parcel (see parcel page), does not apply to export ocean containers (see intl page). if u are unsure which page applies ask transport ops before filing anything, dont guess.

2. WHO CAN FILE
- consignee (the customer receiving the goods) can file a customer claim against Larkspur.
- Larkspur transport ops files carrier claims against the carrier. customers never file directly against our carriers, even if the carrier name is on the BOL.
- sales reps can NOT file claims on behalf of customers. they can open a ticket and pass it to claims desk. a sales rep promising a refund on the phone is not a claim decision.
- 3rd party brokers acting for consignee need a signed letter of authority on file first.

3. FILING WINDOW
- claim must be filed within 7 calendar days of the delivery date shown on the signed POD. not the ship date, not the invoice date, the delivery date.
- day 1 = the day after delivery. so delivered on a monday, day 7 is the next monday.
- concealed damage (found after unwrapping) same 7 day rule, no extension. we used to allow 15 days for concealed damage in rev 3.x, that was removed in rev 4.0. old emails that mention 15 days are out of date.
- the only extension is if our claims portal was down, and ops posts a notice with new deadline. no portal outage notice was issued in the current period.

4. WHAT COUNTS AS A TEMPERATURE EXCURSION
- chilled lanes: set point 0 to 4 C. an excursion = reefer download or data logger shows product air above 4.0 C for MORE THAN 45 continuous minutes.
- frozen lanes: set point -18 C or colder. excursion = above -15.0 C for more than 30 continuous minutes.
- door-open spikes during unloading are excluded if under 20 min total.
- a single reading above threshold is not an excursion. a bunch of short spikes that each reset below threshold do not add up, the rule is continuous minutes.
- if the reefer unit log and our independent data logger disagree, the independent logger wins.

5. PAYABLE COMPONENTS (only when claim is APPROVED)
when a claim is approved the following can be reimbursed, each separately:
 a) product value at invoice price (not retail, not replacement cost)
 b) freight charge refund for the affected pallets, pro rata by pallet count
 c) disposal / destruction fee, only if destruction was ordered or approved by Larkspur QA in writing
 d) re-delivery cost if a replacement load is sent at customer request
none of these are payable on a denied claim. a denied claim pays zero, including disposal. customers sometimes destroy stock first and then ask for disposal fee, if the claim is denied the disposal cost stays with the customer.

6. EXCLUSIONS (claim is denied if any applies)
- E1 late filing (outside 7 days per s.3)
- E2 clean POD: consignee signed POD with no exception notation for visible damage. visible damage means stuff a person could see at the dock, crushed corners, leaking cases, broken wrap. concealed damage is not hit by E2.
- E3 shipper-packed pallet with no independent data logger, temperature claims only. (if Larkspur packed it we always put a logger, so E3 is mostly for co-packer and customer-return loads)
- E4 no excursion per s.4 (temperature claims)
- E5 product accepted at dock after its best-before date
- E6 short-ship claims where seal number on arrival matches seal on BOL AND piece count was signed as correct

7. DECISIONS + CODES
claims desk records one of: APPROVED / PARTIAL / DENIED / PENDING. PENDING must be resolved within 10 business days. codes on denial reference exclusion (E1..E6). goodwill credits issued by sales are tracked separately under GW- numbers and are NOT claims, they dont change a claim status. if a GW credit exists on the same order the claim can still be denied.

8. CARRIER RECOVERY
when a customer claim is approved, transport ops tries to recover from the carrier within 30 days. recovery success doesnt change what the customer gets. if customer claim is denied we usually dont chase the carrier, except where we think the carrier caused a loss we ate ourselves.

9. ESCALATION
customer can appeal a denial once, within 14 days of the denial notice, with NEW evidence. repeating the same argument isnt an appeal. appeals go to Head of Transport Ops. appeal outcomes are logged in Appendix B (not reproduced here, see sharepoint).

4. RENTAL PERIOD
4.1 rental period starts at gate-out time printed on the equipment interchange receipt (EIR) and ends at gate-in time on the return EIR.
4.2 daily rate is charged per started 24h block. so gate-out 09:00 mon and gate-in 10:00 wed = 3 blocks (not 2).
4.3 grace period: a return up to 2 hours after the end of the last full block that was pre-booked is not charged an extra block. grace applies only to the final block, and only if the renter pre-booked a fixed return date in the booking.
4.4 open-ended rentals (no fixed return date) get no grace period at all.

5. LATE RETURN
5.1 if equipment is returned after the booked return time plus any grace in 4.3, a late fee of 1.5x daily rate applies for each started 24h block of lateness.
5.2 late fee replaces, and is not in addition to, the normal daily rate for those blocks.
5.3 late fee is waived where Saltmarsh closed the return depot on the booked return day (public holiday or depot notice).

6. CONDITION ON RETURN
6.1 renter returns equipment in same condition as gate-out, fair wear and tear excepted.
6.2 fair wear and tear includes: scuffs under 10 cm, normal tire wear, dust, minor floor marks.
6.3 damage fee: assessed by depot inspector on the return EIR. no damage fee can be charged unless damage is recorded on the return EIR with photo reference. damage found later than gate-in is not chargable.
6.4 cleaning fee: flat 85 per unit where the inspector records 'residue', 'odour' or 'debris' on the return EIR.
6.5 reefer units: fuel fee charged at cost + 20% if genset fuel below 3/4 tank on return. fuel level recorded on EIR as fraction.

7. USE RESTRICTIONS
7.1 no sublease or loan of equipment to any third party. no exceptions, written consent from a depot manager doesnt override this, only the Saltmarsh legal team can approve and they dont.
7.2 no hazmat classes 1, 6.2 or 7 in any unit.
7.3 max gross weight as per plate on unit. overweight = fee 250 per incident if a weighbridge ticket shows it.
7.4 units may not leave the country of gate-out without a cross-border addendum.

8.1 invoices due 30 days from invoice date.

BRIGHTWATER FREIGHT HUB - DANGEROUS GOODS ACCEPTANCE & SURCHARGE POLICY
doc DG-POL-07 / rev 11 / approved by Uma Castillo (DG safety lead) / questions to dg-desk
read the whole thing b4 quoting a customer. sales keeps quoting DG fees on stuff thats exempt, costs us deals.

1. SCOPE
applies to all road consolidations departing Brightwater hub (LTL groupage, dedicated FTL are covered under DG-POL-09 instead). covers acceptance, segregation, paperwork and surcharges. air and sea DG not covered, we dont do those.

2. DEFINITIONS (short)
- DG = dangerous goods as per the road DG regs, identified by UN number + class.
- LQ = limited quantity. inner packs under the LQ limit for that UN number, marked with LQ diamond. max 30 kg gross per package.
- EQ = excepted quantity. tiny amounts, EQ mark, max 1 kg / 1 L per package typically.
- 1.1.3.6 threshold = 'small load exemption'. total 'points' per vehicle under 1000 = no orange plates, no ADR driver cert needed. points = qty x multiplier for transport category (cat 1 x50, cat 2 x3, cat 3 x1, cat 4 x0).
- Section II lithium = lithium batteries packed in or with equipment, meeting sec II of packing instruction, lithium mark only, no class 9 label.

3. WHAT WE DONT ACCEPT AT ALL
- class 1 explosives (any division except 1.4S, see 3a)
- class 6.2 infectious substances
- class 7 radioactive
- any damaged or leaking DG package
- DG without a DG note / transport doc
3a. 1.4S (e.g. small arms cartridges, some airbag inflators) is accepted, but gets DG handling surcharge and must be booked 48h ahead.

4. SURCHARGES
4.1 DG handling surcharge: 45 per consignment for fully regulated DG (not LQ, not EQ, not sec II lithium).
4.2 ADR vehicle surcharge: 120 per consignment when the vehicle load of the shipment on its own takes points to 1000 or more, requiring plated vehicle + ADR driver. (we calculate per consignment for billing even though its really a vehicle thing, see 4.2a)
4.2a if a single consignment is under 1000 points but the hub combines it with others and the vehicle goes over, the customer is NOT charged 4.2. thats our planning cost.
4.3 segregation surcharge: 60 when the consignment itself contains 2 or more classes that must be segregated from each other per table 7 (e.g. class 3 flammable liquids with class 5.1 oxidisers). segregation from OTHER customers goods is our problem, no charge.
4.4 temp controlled DG (organic peroxides, self-reactive w/ control temp): 200. we rarely take these.
4.5 LQ and EQ: no DG surcharges of any kind under 4.1-4.4. LQ over 8 t gross per vehicle needs LQ vehicle marks, still no charge to customer.
4.6 Section II lithium: no surcharge. section I lithium (class 9 labelled) = fully regulated, 4.1 applies.

5. PAPERWORK
- DG note with UN number, proper shipping name, class, packing group, qty, tunnel code.
- LQ: no DG note needed for road, but we ask for a declaration on the CMR 'LQ' line so we can count tonnage.
- sec II lithium: no DG note, but lithium mark on package.
- missing docs = booking rejected at gate, no fee, customer rebooks.

6. BOOKING LEAD TIMES
- fully regulated DG: 24h
- 1.4S: 48h
- LQ / EQ / sec II: same as general cargo

7. SEGREGATION TABLE 7 (extract, for 4.3)
class 3 vs 5.1: segregate
class 8 vs 4.3: segregate
class 2.1 vs 5.1: segregate
class 3 vs 8: compatible (no segregation) in most cases
class 3 vs 9: compatible
class 8 vs 9: compatible

8. WORKED EXAMPLES (sales training)
ex A: customer ships 20 x 5L paint (UN1263, class 3, PG III, cat 3) as fully regulated, 100 L total. points 100 x 1 = 100. under 1000. charges: 4.1 = 45. no 4.2. no 4.3 (single class).
ex B: customer ships 1,200 L of UN1203 petrol (class 3, cat 2). points 1200 x 3 = 3600. charges: 4.1 = 45 + 4.2 = 120 = 165.
ex C: pool chemicals mixed load, class 5.1 oxidiser + class 3 solvent in same consignment: 4.1 + 4.3, + 4.2 if points >= 1000.
ex D: LQ aerosols, 600 kg: nothing. 0 surcharge.

9. CURRENT BOOKING FOR REVIEW (dg-desk queue, pasted by Zoltan Kowalski, ops planner)
booking BRW-44871, customer: Hollowmere Cleaning Supplies
collection mon, delivery tue, LTL groupage
lines:
 L1 - 40 cartons hand sanitiser gel, UN1170 ethanol solution, class 3, PG II, packed as LQ (500 ml bottles x 12 per carton, LQ diamond marked, 7.2 kg gross per carton). total 288 kg
 L2 - 16 cartons toilet descaler, UN1789 hydrochloric acid solution, class 8, PG III, packed LQ (1 L bottles x 12, LQ marked, 13.5 kg gross per carton). total 216 kg
 L3 - 6 cordless floor scrubbers with lithium ion battery installed, marked lithium mark, sec II per shipper declaration, no class 9 label
 L4 - 30 cartons microfibre cloths, not DG
total DG gross (LQ) 504 kg
shipper note on CMR: 'LQ 504 kg'. no DG note attached.

Zoltan comments: sales quoted 45 + 60 because 'two DG classes, acid and alcohol, gotta segregate'. customer disputing. also sales thinks the scrubbers need class 9 fee. I think the whole quote is wrong, pls confirm. hub will combine this with a Kovanda Chemicals fully regulated load of UN1203 petrol 1,100 L on the same trailer tue, which puts the trailer over 1000 pts. planning aware.

10. DG DESK RESPONSE (Uma Castillo, tue 08:10)
Zoltan - agree, quote wrong. L1 and L2 both LQ per s.2 (packs marked, cartons under 30 kg). per 4.5 LQ gets no surcharge under 4.1-4.4, that includes segregation, and anyway class 3 vs 8 is compatible per table 7. L3 is sec II lithium, 4.6 no surcharge, no class 9. L4 not DG. trailer going over 1000 is from the Kovanda petrol, 4.2a says Hollowmere not charged. no DG note needed for LQ on road, CMR LQ line fine. booking lead time normal. pls reissue quote with DG surcharges = 0. accept booking.

fyi for sales - common mistakes:
 1) seeing two class numbers and adding 4.3. check table 7 AND check whether its LQ.
 2) charging 4.2 because the truck went over 1000. only if THIS consignment does it by itself.

IN THE COUNTY COURT OF MARLOW COUNTY, CIVIL DIVISION

SVEN RAHMAN,
Plaintiff,
v.
BRIGHTWATER MOTORS LLC, d/b/a Brightwater Kestrel of Marlow,
Defendant.

Case No. 24-CV-03817

DEFENDANT BRIGHTWATER MOTORS LLC'S RESPONSE TO PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR PARTIAL SUMMARY JUDGMENT, WITH INCORPORATED STATEMENT OF POSITION ON REQUESTED RELIEF

(Excerpt: Sections I through VII, Exhibit C, and Certificate of Service)

May it please the Court:

Defendant Brightwater Motors LLC ('Brightwater' or 'Defendant'), by and through its undersigned counsel, most respectfully submits this Response to the Motion for Partial Summary Judgment filed by Plaintiff Sven Rahman ('Plaintiff' or 'Mr. Rahman'). Defendant wishes at the outset to extend its sincere gratitude to the Court for its patience in granting the brief extension requested on March 29, and to thank Plaintiff and his counsel for their unfailing courtesy throughout discovery. Defendant is keenly aware that Mr. Rahman has been a loyal customer of the dealership, having purchased two prior vehicles from it, and Defendant would like the Court to know that nothing in this Response is intended to diminish the genuine regret the dealership feels about the difficulties Mr. Rahman experienced. Defendant simply and humbly asks that the Court consider the record as a whole.

I. INTRODUCTION

This matter arises from Plaintiff's purchase, on September 14 of last year, of a new Kestrel TR-400 pickup truck in the Trailhand trim, equipped with the 3.2-liter engine (the 'Vehicle'). Plaintiff alleges that he was told the Vehicle could tow up to 7,500 pounds, that he relied on that representation in purchasing a travel trailer, and that the Vehicle's transmission overheated and failed on October 22 while he was towing that trailer on the Hollis Pass grade. Plaintiff seeks rescission of the purchase, refund of certain fees and add-on charges, reimbursement of diagnostic costs, punitive damages, and attorney fees.

Defendant would most respectfully note that the parties' disagreements are narrower than the pleadings might suggest. As set out in Section VI below, Defendant has, in the spirit of good faith and with the greatest respect for Mr. Rahman, elected not to contest several items of relief. Defendant does, however, continue to oppose certain other items, and it very politely asks the Court to deny summary judgment as to those.

II. STATEMENT OF UNDISPUTED FACTS (AS RESPONDED TO BY DEFENDANT)

Defendant responds to Plaintiff's numbered statement of facts as follows, and apologizes in advance for the length of certain responses, which it has tried to keep as brief as candor allows.

1. Plaintiff's Paragraph 1 (date of purchase). Admitted. The purchase agreement was executed on September 14.

2. Plaintiff's Paragraph 2 (identity of Vehicle). Admitted. The Vehicle is a Kestrel TR-400, Trailhand trim, 3.2-liter engine, four-wheel drive, with a 6.5-foot bed. Defendant would gently add that it is not disputed by either party that the Vehicle was not equipped with the optional Max Tow Package at the time of sale, and that no such package was installed at any time afterward.

3. Plaintiff's Paragraph 3 (salesperson). Admitted that the transaction was handled by sales consultant Mr. Oren Pellwood, who has been with Brightwater for eleven years and who, Defendant would respectfully mention, has asked counsel to convey his personal apologies to Mr. Rahman for any confusion.

4. Plaintiff's Paragraph 4 (window sticker). Denied. Defendant denies that its salesperson failed to provide the Monroney window sticker. The sticker was affixed to the Vehicle on the lot and a copy was placed in the deal jacket; Plaintiff's own initials appear on the delivery checklist line reading 'Window sticker reviewed with customer.' Defendant most humbly submits that this fact is not reasonably in dispute.

5. Plaintiff's Paragraph 5 (the brochure). Admitted in part. Defendant admits that the 2024 TR-400 general sales brochure displayed in the showroom states that the TR-400 line 'tows up to 7,500 lbs.' Defendant respectfully notes that the same page of the brochure carries a footnote reading 'When properly equipped. See dealer for trim-specific ratings.' Defendant does not ask the Court to decide at this stage whether that footnote was adequate, and it is grateful for the opportunity to address the point at trial if the Court should wish.

6. Plaintiff's Paragraph 6 (the revised specification sheet). Defendant would very respectfully respond as follows. In August of last year, the manufacturer, Kestrel Truck Company, issued a revised trim-specific specification sheet for the TR-400 (the 'Revised Sheet,' attached as Exhibit C). Defendant does not dispute that it did not furnish the Revised Sheet to Plaintiff prior to the execution of the purchase agreement on September 14. Defendant's records reflect that the Revised Sheet was received by the dealership's sales office on August 30 but had not yet been distributed to the sales floor binders at the time of Plaintiff's purchase. Defendant regrets this lapse most sincerely.

7. Plaintiff's Paragraph 7 (the trailer). Admitted that Plaintiff purchased, from an unrelated seller, a travel trailer with a manufacturer's dry weight of 5,400 pounds. Defendant would kindly note that Plaintiff's own weigh-station ticket of October 22, produced in discovery, reflects a loaded trailer weight of 6,200 pounds.

8. Plaintiff's Paragraph 8 (transmission failure). Admitted that the Vehicle's transmission overheated on October 22 and that the Vehicle was towed to Brightwater's service department on October 23.

9. Plaintiff's Paragraph 9 (diagnostic charge). Admitted that Plaintiff was charged a diagnostic fee of $310.00 on October 24, and that Plaintiff paid it.

10. Plaintiff's Paragraph 10 (warranty denial). Admitted that the manufacturer's warranty administrator declined coverage on the ground that the Vehicle had been operated above its rated towing capacity. Defendant takes no position on the correctness of the manufacturer's decision and would not wish to be understood as endorsing it.

11. Plaintiff's Paragraph 11 (dealer add-ons). Admitted that the purchase agreement included a 'Brightwater Protection Bundle' (paint sealant, interior fabric guard, nitrogen-filled tires and wheel locks) priced at $1,450.00.

12. Plaintiff's Paragraph 12 (late fee). Admitted that a late fee of $75.00 was assessed on Plaintiff's November payment through Brightwater's in-house finance arm, during the period when the Vehicle was out of service.

III. THE MANUFACTURER'S RATINGS

Defendant would most respectfully direct the Court's attention to Exhibit C, the Revised Sheet. Defendant appreciates that specification sheets are not the most engaging reading, and it thanks the Court in advance for its forbearance.

The Revised Sheet lists four configurations of the TR-400. Defendant has reproduced the relevant table below. Only one of these configurations corresponds to the Vehicle. Defendant would note, with respect, that the 7,500-pound figure appearing in the brochure corresponds to the Trailhand trim only when the Max Tow Package is installed, and that the 8,900-pound figure sometimes discussed in online forums corresponds to the Summit trim with the 3.8-liter engine, which the Vehicle is not.

IV. ARGUMENT: GENUINE DISPUTES OF MATERIAL FACT REMAIN AS TO RELIANCE

Defendant would most humbly submit that summary judgment on Plaintiff's misrepresentation count is not appropriate because the record contains conflicting evidence regarding what Mr. Pellwood said to Plaintiff. Mr. Pellwood's deposition testimony is that, when Plaintiff asked about towing, Mr. Pellwood said 'the TR-400 can do up to seventy-five hundred, but I'd want to check the exact number for this one.' Plaintiff's testimony is that Mr. Pellwood said 'this truck does seventy-five hundred, no problem.' Defendant does not suggest that either witness is being anything other than honest; memories of conversations fade, and Defendant has the greatest respect for Mr. Rahman's recollection. But the difference is material, and Defendant respectfully submits that a fact-finder should be permitted to weigh it.

Defendant would further note, with apologies for belaboring the point, that the question of reliance is complicated by the fact that the loaded trailer weight of 6,200 pounds would have exceeded the Vehicle's rating whether or not Plaintiff had been told 7,500 pounds; it is the rating itself, not the conversation, that governs the warranty question. Defendant raises this not to shift blame to Plaintiff, which it would never wish to do, but because the causal chain is a matter for trial.

V. ARGUMENT: PLAINTIFF'S RESCISSION CLAIM IS NOT RIPE FOR SUMMARY DISPOSITION

Defendant most respectfully opposes Plaintiff's request for full rescission of the purchase agreement at this stage. The purchase price of $48,960.00 was financed in part through a third-party lender, Coastline Auto Credit, which is not a party to this action. Defendant would gently observe that rescission would require an unwinding of that financing, and it is not clear to Defendant, with respect, that the Court could grant complete relief without the lender's participation. Defendant would be glad to cooperate in any joinder the Court deems proper.

Defendant also notes, without any wish to be ungracious, that the Vehicle has been driven approximately 3,140 miles since delivery and that the transmission has since been replaced under a goodwill arrangement described in Section VI.

VI. DEFENDANT'S POSITION ON EACH ITEM OF REQUESTED RELIEF

In the interest of narrowing the issues and of honoring the long relationship between Brightwater and Mr. Rahman, Defendant sets out its position on each item of relief below. Defendant would ask the Court's indulgence for the precision of the phrasing, which counsel has adopted so that there can be no misunderstanding.

(A) Refund of the Brightwater Protection Bundle ($1,450.00). Defendant does not oppose this request. Defendant will refund the full $1,450.00 within fourteen days of any order so providing, or sooner if Plaintiff would prefer.

(B) Reversal of the $75.00 late fee. Defendant does not contest that the late fee should be reversed. Brightwater's finance arm has already been instructed to credit the fee, and Defendant apologizes that this was not done sooner.

(C) Reimbursement of the $310.00 diagnostic fee. It is not the case that Defendant refuses to reimburse the diagnostic fee. Defendant will reimburse it in full.

(D) Goodwill transmission replacement. Although Plaintiff has not requested this as relief, Defendant wishes the Court to be aware that it replaced the transmission at no charge on January 9, and that it does not now seek, and will not in the future seek, any payment for that work.

(E) Full rescission of the purchase agreement. Defendant opposes this request for the reasons set out in Section V. Defendant would not be unwilling to discuss a negotiated trade-in arrangement, but it cannot, with respect, consent to rescission at this stage.

(F) Punitive damages. Defendant opposes this request. Defendant most respectfully submits that nothing in the record would permit a finding of malice or reckless indifference; the failure to distribute the Revised Sheet was an administrative oversight, which Defendant has candidly acknowledged.

(G) Attorney fees. Defendant opposes Plaintiff's request for attorney fees in the amount claimed ($22,800.00). Defendant does not suggest that Plaintiff's counsel's hours were anything other than genuinely incurred, but it respectfully submits that fees are not recoverable under the counts on which summary judgment is sought.

VII. CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons, Defendant Brightwater Motors LLC most respectfully requests that the Court (1) enter judgment in Plaintiff's favor as to items (A), (B) and (C) of Section VI, to which Defendant consents; (2) deny Plaintiff's Motion as to items (E), (F) and (G); and (3) set the remaining issues for trial at the Court's earliest convenience. Defendant once more thanks the Court for its time and consideration.

Respectfully submitted,

Dalia Kaur
Kaur & Whitfield, Attorneys at Law
Counsel for Defendant Brightwater Motors LLC

---

KESTREL TRUCK COMPANY
TR-400 SERIES: TRIM-SPECIFIC SPECIFICATION SHEET (REVISED)
Revision 3, issued August 22
Supersedes Revision 2 in its entirety

Dear Valued Kestrel Retail Partner,

Thank you so very much for your continued partnership. We are pleased to provide this revised specification sheet and would kindly ask that it be placed in all sales-floor reference binders at your earliest convenience. SECTION 1. POWERTRAIN

Worksite trim: 2.7-liter inline-four turbo, 270 hp, 8-speed automatic, rear-wheel drive standard, four-wheel drive optional.
Trailhand trim: 3.2-liter V6, 310 hp, 8-speed automatic, four-wheel drive standard.

Summit trim: 3.8-liter V6 twin-turbo, 400 hp, 10-speed automatic, four-wheel drive standard.

SECTION 2. TOWING AND PAYLOAD (SAE J2807)

Configuration | Max Trailer Weight | Max Tongue Weight | Payload | GCWR
Worksite 2.7L | 4,200 lbs | 420 lbs | 1,640 lbs | 9,300 lbs
Trailhand 3.2L | 5,000 lbs | 500 lbs | 1,520 lbs | 10,400 lbs
Trailhand 3.2L + Max Tow Package | 7,500 lbs | 750 lbs | 1,480 lbs | 12,900 lbs
Summit 3.8L | 8,900 lbs | 890 lbs | 1,410 lbs | 14,600 lbs

SECTION 3. DIMENSIONS

Summit 3.8L: 16 city / 21 highway.

SECTION 5. IDENTIFYING THE MAX TOW PACKAGE

A vehicle lacking all three of these is not a Max Tow Package vehicle.

Powertrain coverage does not extend to damage caused by operation beyond the configuration's rated trailer weight or GCWR. We kindly ask that retail partners review the correct trim-specific rating with each customer at delivery.

#2 chiara_mensah_boxoffice

Item 1, the double refunds.

So this started in late September. Our membership coordinator processes an upgrade the normal way: open the member record, click Upgrade, choose the new tier, and Copperleaf calculates a prorated credit for the old tier and a charge for the new tier. Normally you get one refund line and one charge line. What we were seeing is two refund lines, same amount, a few seconds apart, and BOTH of them actually settling on the member's card. The member gets, say, $38.40 back twice and then pays the $120 Family price once.

We found 27 of these between 23 September and 18 October. Most members didn't notice, a handful emailed us being very nice about it ("I think you gave me too much money back?") and one emailed us being very suspicious about it ("is this a scam"). We've now clawed back most of them by asking nicely, and just written off the rest because honestly chasing a retired schoolteacher for $22 is not a good look.

I opened a support case with Copperleaf, CL-7741. I will let the Copperleaf person answer for themselves because I believe one of their support folks is on this forum, but to be clear up front: our coordinator did NOT click the button twice. We checked this because it was the first thing everyone asked. We screen-recorded her doing one upgrade on a test member and it produced two refund lines from one click.

@jonas_delgado_ops yes we checked the dropdown, it was correctly on "Refund - prorated membership credit". One click, two lines. We have the video. Anyway.

Item 2, the Brookfield school group. This one I want to lay out carefully because the story has been retold in our building so many times that people now believe totally different versions of it, and one of our trustees at the last meeting said "the school cancelled on us and then complained," which is NOT what happened, and I want it written down properly somewhere.

The booking was SG-2291. Brookfield Middle School, teacher lead Aiden O'Neill, 62 students plus 6 adults, originally booked for Tuesday 14 October, the "Ships and Storms" guided program in the morning then the lightship in the afternoon.

Around 7 October, Mr O'Neill emailed our schools inbox. I have the email. The relevant bit is:

> "Hi, there's a bus drivers' strike threatened for the week of the 13th. If we can't get buses we'll have to cancel altogether, which I really don't want to do, the kids have been looking forward to it for weeks. Is there any chance of moving us to the following Tuesday, the 21st, instead? Same program, same numbers."

Note "if we can't get buses we'll have to cancel". He did not cancel. He asked to move it. Tomasz on our schools desk replied the same day saying yes, the 21st was open, and he'd move it.

Tomasz then went into Copperleaf, opened SG-2291, and used the "Change date" function to move it from 14 Oct to 21 Oct. That's the normal way to do it. It's not a cancel-and-rebook, it's an edit of the same booking — same booking number, same deposit, same everything, just a new date.

And then, a few minutes later, Mr O'Neill received an automated email from our system with the subject line "Your booking SG-2291 has been cancelled" and body text saying the booking was cancelled and any deposit would be refunded within 10 business days.

He, very reasonably, lost his mind a bit. He called the front desk, got our weekend person who didn't know anything, and the weekend person looked at the screen, saw the booking was for the 21st, and said "it's showing as booked for the 21st?" and Mr O'Neill said "then why did you send me a cancellation" and nobody could answer him.

Tomasz called him back first thing Monday, apologised, sent a manual confirmation for the 21st, and... the group came on the 21st. All 62 kids. I was there. They loved the lightship, one kid threw up on the gangway, it was a normal school visit. The deposit was never refunded because nothing was ever cancelled — the booking status in Copperleaf has said "Confirmed — Rescheduled" the whole time, and the audit log for SG-2291 shows one event: "date_changed 2025-10-14 -> 2025-10-21 by t.castillo". There's no "cancelled" event in the log at all.

So to be very clear for anyone skimming: nobody cancelled SG-2291. Not the school, not us, not the system. It was moved. The system just sent the wrong email template.

Separately, and this is where the trustee's version comes from I think, a DIFFERENT school did actually cancel on us that same week. SG-2288, St. Brigid's Primary, 30 kids, booked for Thursday 16 October. Their head teacher emailed on 9 October saying they were cancelling due to the strike and weren't going to reschedule this term. Tomasz processed that as a real cancellation, deposit refunded per policy. So there WAS a school that cancelled because of the strike, it just wasn't Brookfield. I think people merged the two in their heads.
