Bramblewood Mutual Insurance - Homeowners Standard Plus - Policy Terms (excerpt)

This excerpt is provided for reference and does not replace the full policy wording. In the event of conflict, the full policy wording issued to you prevails. We know nobody reads this. We wrote it anyway.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS

1.1 'You' and 'your' mean the named policyholder shown on the declarations page and members of your household who normally live at the insured property.

1.2 'We', 'us' and 'our' mean Bramblewood Mutual Insurance.

1.3 'Insured property' means the dwelling at the address shown on the declarations page, including permanently attached fixtures and fittings, and the land within its boundaries.

1.4 'Sudden and accidental' means an event that happens abruptly, without warning, and is not expected or intended by you. A slow leak that has been occurring for weeks is not sudden merely because you noticed it suddenly.

1.5 'Additional living expenses' (ALE) means the reasonable increase in your normal living costs that you necessarily incur because the insured property is not fit to live in following a covered loss.

1.6 'Deductible' means the amount you must pay toward each claim before we pay, as shown on your declarations page.

1.7 'Endorsement' means a written change to this policy that adds, removes or modifies coverage.

1.8 'Household companion' means a domestic cat, dog, rabbit or other pet normally kept at the insured property, excluding livestock and any animal kept for business purposes.

SECTION 2 - WHAT THIS POLICY COVERS

2.1 We cover physical loss of or damage to the insured property caused by an insured peril, subject to the conditions, limits and exclusions of this policy.

2.2 Insured perils include fire, lightning, explosion, smoke, storm, hail, theft, vandalism, impact by vehicles, and sudden and accidental discharge of water, as described in Section 4.

2.3 This policy does not cover wear and tear, gradual deterioration, or maintenance you should reasonably have carried out. We are an insurer, not a handyman.

SECTION 3 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS

3.1 We do not cover loss caused by flood, meaning the overflow of natural bodies of water or surface water from outside the dwelling, unless you have purchased the Flood Extension endorsement.

3.2 We do not cover loss caused by your deliberate act or the deliberate act of anyone living with you.

3.3 We do not cover mould, rot or fungus, except where it results directly from a covered sudden and accidental discharge of water and is discovered and reported within 14 days of the discharge.

3.4 We do not cover loss that occurs while the insured property has been unoccupied for more than 60 consecutive days, unless you told us beforehand and we agreed in writing.

3.5 We do not cover damage caused by pets you own, including chewing, scratching and 'accidents', however much you love them.

SECTION 4 - WATER DAMAGE

4.1 This section applies to damage caused by water escaping from plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, fire protection systems or domestic appliances inside the dwelling.

4.2 We cover damage to the insured property caused by the sudden and accidental discharge, leakage or overflow of water from a plumbing system or appliance, including the reasonable cost of tearing out and replacing any part of the building necessary to repair the system from which the water escaped.

4.3 We will also pay the reasonable cost of emergency repairs to stop further damage, including an emergency plumber's call-out, provided you take reasonable steps to minimise the loss, such as turning off the water supply.

4.4 We do not cover the cost of repairing or replacing the defective pipe or appliance itself beyond the section necessary to stop the discharge, unless the defect was itself caused by an insured peril.

4.5 We do not cover water damage resulting from continuous or repeated seepage or leakage over a period of 14 days or more.

4.6 We do not cover damage from frozen pipes if the dwelling was unheated and you failed to drain the water system, unless the dwelling was occupied at the time.

SECTION 5 - HOW WE SETTLE DWELLING CLAIMS

5.1 We will pay the reasonable cost to repair or replace the damaged part of the dwelling with materials of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, provided repairs are completed within 12 months of the loss.

5.2 If repairs are not completed within 12 months, we will pay the actual cash value of the damage at the date of loss.

5.3 The dwelling deductible applies once per occurrence to the dwelling portion of the claim.

5.4 We are not obliged to match undamaged areas unless it is not reasonably possible to obtain matching materials, in which case we will pay to replace a continuous area in a reasonable line of sight.

SECTION 6 - ADDITIONAL LIVING EXPENSES

6.1 If a covered loss makes the insured property unfit to live in, we will pay additional living expenses as follows:
(a) ALE is payable only for the period reasonably required to repair the dwelling or for you to settle elsewhere, whichever is shorter.
(b) Hotel or temporary accommodation costs must be reasonable having regard to the size and standard of your normal home and the availability of accommodation in the area. Accommodation that accepts your household companion is considered reasonable even where it costs more than comparable accommodation that does not.
(c) ALE does not include the cost of boarding pets unless you have the Household Companion endorsement (HCE-1 or HCE-2).
(d) ALE is limited to 30 days under Standard Plus, and to 90 days under Premier.

6.2 We will pay for reasonable additional costs of meals only to the extent they exceed your normal food costs. Please do not send us your normal grocery bill. We have seen it. It is not an additional cost.

6.3 We will pay reasonable additional mileage if your temporary accommodation is further from your workplace than your home.

6.4 ALE and amounts payable under the Household Companion endorsement are not subject to the dwelling deductible.

6.5 Receipts are required for all ALE claims. Estimates, verbal descriptions, and heartfelt essays are appreciated but not payable.

SECTION 7 - CLAIMS PROCEDURE

7.1 You must report a loss to us as soon as reasonably possible, and in any case within 30 days.

7.2 You must take reasonable steps to prevent further damage. We will pay the reasonable cost of those steps as part of the claim.

7.3 Where you obtain your own contractor's quote, we will settle on your quote if it is within 10% of our preferred-vendor estimate. If it exceeds our estimate by more than 10%, we will pay our estimate plus 10%, unless you show a reasonable justification for the difference.

7.4 You must provide us with photographs, receipts, invoices and any other documents we reasonably request. You may submit them through our online portal or, where the portal is unavailable, by email to the address we provide.

7.5 We may inspect the insured property. You must give us reasonable access.

7.6 We will aim to make a decision on your claim within 30 days of receiving all the information we need.

SECTION 8 - LIMITS

8.1 The maximum amount we will pay for dwelling damage is the dwelling limit shown on your declarations page.

8.2 ALE is subject to the time limit in 6.1(d) and to a monetary limit of 20% of the dwelling limit.

8.3 Endorsement limits are shown in the endorsement wording.

SECTION 9 - ENDORSEMENTS (SUMMARY)

9.1 Flood Extension (FE-1): extends cover to flood as defined in 3.1, subject to a separate deductible.

9.2 Household Companion endorsement (HCE-1): covers veterinary costs for injuries to your household companion caused directly by an insured peril, up to $1,500 per occurrence.

9.3 Household Companion endorsement (HCE-2): includes everything in HCE-1 and additionally covers boarding costs for your household companion while ALE is payable, up to $50 per night per animal, for no more than 30 nights. Boarding is covered only for nights your household companion cannot reasonably stay with you in your temporary accommodation.

9.4 Home Office endorsement (HO-B): covers business equipment at the insured property up to $5,000. Laptops, monitors and other equipment used for work are not covered under the standard contents section without this endorsement, regardless of how important the spreadsheet on them was.

9.5 Vehicle Rental Add-on (VR-1): not available on homeowners policies. We mention it here only because people ask. The answer is no.

SECTION 10 - DISPUTES

10.1 If you disagree with our decision, you may ask for an internal review by writing to our Claims Review team within 60 days of our decision.

10.2 If you remain dissatisfied, you may refer the matter to the independent insurance ombudsman service shown on your declarations page.

10.3 Nothing in this section affects your statutory rights.

SECTION 11 - CANCELLATION AND NON-RENEWAL

11.1 You may cancel this policy at any time by telling us in writing. If you cancel mid-term, we will refund the unused portion of your premium less an administration fee of $35, provided no claim has been paid in the current term.

11.2 If you tell us you do not want your policy to renew, it will end at midnight on the last day of the current term and no refund is due. We will confirm in writing.

11.3 Where a claim has been paid in the current term, mid-term cancellation will not result in a refund of premium.

11.4 We may decline to renew your policy by giving you at least 30 days' written notice before the renewal date.

11.5 Premiums on renewal are calculated using our current rating factors and may increase or decrease. Any increase will be shown on your renewal notice. We call this transparency. You may call it something else.

SECTION 12 - GENERAL CONDITIONS

12.1 You must tell us about any change in circumstances that might affect your cover, including changes in occupancy, major renovations, or starting a business at home.

12.2 If you make a fraudulent claim, we will not pay it, we may cancel your policy, and we may keep any premium paid.

12.3 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction shown on your declarations page.

12.4 If any part of this policy is found to be unenforceable, the remaining parts continue in effect.

state:
TIDEWATER FOODS — ACCOUNTS PAYABLE TEAM
Monthly Review Meeting: Minutes, with Appendices
Meeting date: Tuesday, 11 March
Location: Conference Room B ("the Pantry"), with two colleagues joining by video
Minutes taken by: Wanjiru Tanaka (with sincere apologies in advance for any errors; corrections are warmly invited)

---------------------------------------------------------------

ATTENDEES

- Beatriz Moreau, AP Manager (chair)
- Esi Castillo, Senior AP Specialist
- Aiden Delgado, AP Specialist (vendor reconciliations)
- Wanjiru Alvarez, Vendor Master Data Coordinator
- Rosa Haddad, AP Specialist (dispute resolution and correspondence), by video
- Wanjiru Tanaka, AP Assistant (minutes), in the room

Apologies received from: the Treasury liaison, who very kindly sent a note saying she was at the bank's quarterly review and would read these minutes afterwards. We thank her for letting us know so graciously.

---------------------------------------------------------------

1. OPENING AND WELCOME

Beatriz opened the meeting at 9:32 a.m. and thanked everyone most sincerely for making the time, particularly given that the week before had been, in her words, "a genuinely heroic effort on the February close, for which I cannot thank you all enough." She asked that her gratitude be recorded in the minutes, and the minute-taker is very happy to do so.

Beatriz also offered a special thank-you to Rosa for dialling in despite having a head cold, and asked her please not to feel obliged to stay on the call for the full meeting if she felt unwell. Rosa thanked Beatriz for her kindness and said she was feeling much better and would be delighted to stay.

Esi asked whether it might be possible, if nobody minded terribly, to move the item about the new invoice software (item 6) slightly later in the agenda, because she was hoping the IT colleague might send over some figures during the meeting. Everyone was very agreeable to this and the agenda was adjusted accordingly.

The minute-taker would like to note, with apologies, that coffee ran out at approximately 9:50 a.m. and she will do her very best to ensure the pot is refilled before next month's session.

---------------------------------------------------------------

2. REVIEW OF PREVIOUS MINUTES (11 February)

The minutes of the February meeting were reviewed. Aiden very politely pointed out that the February minutes had listed the Bluefin Health remittance address as the old Harborview Road address, whereas the vendor had in fact moved to the Quayside Park address in January. He apologised for raising it and said he was sure it was just a small slip. Wanjiru Tanaka thanked Aiden for catching this and apologised for the error; she will correct the February minutes and recirculate them.

With that single correction, the February minutes were accepted. Beatriz thanked everyone for their careful reading.

Outstanding items carried from February were walked through briefly:

(a) The February action to "chase the missing W-9 from the linen supplier" was completed by Esi on 19 February. Beatriz thanked her.

(b) The February action to "investigate whether we could move the Thursday payment run to Wednesday" was discussed. Esi explained, very apologetically, that she had looked into it and that, were we to move the run to Wednesday, the bank's cut-off would give us about four fewer hours of approval time, which she thought might put pressure on the approvers. She said that if the team felt strongly she would of course be happy to pursue it, but her gentle recommendation was to keep Thursday. Everyone agreed, and the item was closed with thanks. No change to the payment run day has been made.

(c) The February action for Aiden to reconcile the Harbor Health statement was reported complete. See item 3 below for the resulting discussion.

---------------------------------------------------------------

3. VENDOR REVIEW — HARBOR HEALTH

Aiden presented the reconciliation of the Harbor Health statement dated 28 February. He thanked Harbor Health's receivables contact, whom he described as "unfailingly courteous," for sending the statement promptly.

Summary as presented:

- Harbor Health statement balance: $31,605.00
- Our open AP ledger for Harbor Health: $31,605.00
- Difference: nil

Aiden was pleased to report that the statement and our ledger agreed exactly for the first time in about five months, and he thanked Esi for her help in clearing the old unapplied payment from October. Esi said it was entirely Aiden's doing and that she had merely pointed him to the right report.

Of the open balance, the item for discussion was invoice HH-44718, dated 14 February, for $18,240.00, covering the quarterly occupational health screening for our warehouse staff. Aiden confirmed that:

- the purchase order (PO 7781) was for $18,240.00;
- the goods receipt / service confirmation had been signed off by the warehouse operations lead on 20 February;
- the three-way match was clean, with no price or quantity variance.

Beatriz asked whether anyone had any concerns about HH-44718. Nobody did. Beatriz then said: "In that case, and with thanks to Aiden, I approve HH-44718 for payment, and I'd be grateful if it could go out on this Thursday's run." Esi confirmed she would include it in the Thursday run. The approval was recorded in the AP system by Beatriz during the meeting at 9:58 a.m. (the minute-taker saw the approval confirmation on the shared screen).

Late fee discussion. Rosa raised, very gently, that the prior Harbor Health invoice (HH-43902, for $13,365.00, from December) had been paid eleven days late back in January because of the approver's holiday, and that Harbor Health had added a late fee of $200.45 on the February statement. (This late fee is included within the $31,605.00 balance above.) Rosa said she felt a little awkward asking, but wondered whether we might politely request that Harbor Health waive the fee, given our long relationship and the fact that the delay was a one-off.

Beatriz said she thought that was an excellent idea and asked Rosa to please write to Harbor Health requesting the waiver. Rosa agreed to send the letter by Friday 14 March. (Recorded as an action item — see section 10.)

There was then some discussion about what would happen next. Aiden observed that, if Harbor Health agreed to the waiver, they would presumably issue a credit memo for $200.45, which we would then apply against the open balance. Rosa agreed that this was likely, but stressed that she had not yet written to them and that Harbor Health had certainly not offered anything so far. Beatriz said that, should a credit memo arrive, Aiden should please apply it in the usual way, but that nobody should anticipate it in the ledger until it actually arrived. To be clear for the record: no credit memo from Harbor Health has been received, and none was discussed as having been received.

Esi added, with a small laugh, that had we paid HH-43902 on time we would have saved not only the late fee but also the 1% early-payment discount that Harbor Health offers for payment within ten days, which on $13,365.00 would have been $133.65. She said she wasn't mentioning this to criticise anyone, merely as a reminder of why the new approval-delegation rules were such a kind idea. Beatriz thanked her.

---------------------------------------------------------------

4. VENDOR REVIEW — MERIDIAN OUTFITTERS

Esi presented this item, and she prefaced it by thanking Meridian Outfitters for having been "so patient with us over the uniform re-order muddle in the autumn."

The item for discussion concerned two invoices from Meridian Outfitters for staff uniforms (aprons, non-slip shoes and hairnets for the production line):

- MO-9013, dated 3 February, for $7,486.20
- MO-9031, dated 24 February, for $7,486.20

Esi explained that the two invoices had the same amount, the same PO reference (PO 7702), and the same line items, and that the invoice numbers differed only by a transposition of the last two digits. She said, very carefully, that she did not wish to accuse Meridian of anything and that there might be a perfectly reasonable explanation — for example, a second shipment of the same order, which the production manager had mentioned might happen. However, she thought it had the look of a possible duplicate.

Aiden said that the goods receipt records in the system showed only one delivery against PO 7702, on 5 February, but that the warehouse sometimes recorded split deliveries late, so he could not yet be sure.

Beatriz asked where things stood with each invoice. Esi confirmed:

- MO-9013 was paid on the 13 February run (check #20398... sorry, correction from Esi: it was paid by ACH, reference ACH-0213-114). This payment has cleared.
- MO-9031 is currently sitting in the normal approval queue with a scheduled payment date of 26 March (Net 30 from 24 February).

There was then a fairly long discussion about whether to put MO-9031 on hold. The minute-taker has tried to record it faithfully:

Wanjiru Alvarez asked whether the system would allow a hold to be placed now, pending investigation. Esi said it would, and that she had the access to do so.

Rosa said that, if it did turn out to be a duplicate, the proper thing would be to hold MO-9031 and ask Meridian for a credit or a cancellation of the invoice.

Beatriz said she was reluctant to hold an invoice from a vendor who had been so accommodating without first speaking to them, because a hold would trigger an automated notification to the vendor, and she didn't want Meridian to feel accused. She proposed instead: "Let's have Esi call Meridian first, very politely, to ask whether a second shipment was sent. If Aiden and Esi together confirm it's a duplicate, then we would place MO-9031 on hold and request a cancellation. But until then, let's leave it in the normal queue — there's plenty of time before the 26th."

Everyone agreed with this approach. Esi was asked to call Meridian Outfitters this week. (Recorded as an action item — see section 10.)

Aiden noted, a little ruefully, that had we noticed the resemblance when MO-9031 first arrived on 25 February, we would have held it straight away and saved ourselves this discussion. Beatriz reassured him kindly that it was nobody's fault, since the invoice had arrived during the close.

For absolute clarity, the minute-taker confirmed with Esi at the end of the item: MO-9031 has NOT been placed on hold. It remains in the normal approval queue, unapproved, with a scheduled date of 26 March. No hold, block or payment stop has been applied to any Meridian Outfitters invoice. Esi confirmed this was correct.

MO-9031 was not approved at this meeting.

---------------------------------------------------------------

5. VENDOR REVIEW — BLUEFIN HEALTH

Wanjiru Alvarez presented this item. She began by thanking Bluefin Health for their "lovely, clear communication" regarding their change of address and their new payment terms.

5.1 Change of payment terms

Bluefin Health supplies first-aid consumables and the on-site nurse service for our processing plant. Their letter dated 21 February informed us that, with effect from 1 April, their payment terms would change from Net 30 to Net 45, which they described as a gesture of goodwill in recognition of our long relationship. Wanjiru Alvarez said she thought this was extremely kind of them.

The vendor master record still shows Net 30. Beatriz asked Wanjiru Alvarez to please update the Bluefin Health payment terms in the vendor master to Net 45, effective 1 April, and to attach the letter to the vendor record as supporting documentation. Wanjiru Alvarez agreed to do this by Wednesday 19 March. (Recorded as an action item — see section 10.)

5.2 Credit memo CM-2291

Wanjiru Alvarez reported that Bluefin Health's credit memo CM-2291, for $1,120.00, relating to a batch of expired burn-gel sachets that had been returned in January, was received by post on 4 March. Aiden confirmed that he had matched it to the return authorisation (RA-0117) and applied it against the Bluefin Health open balance on 6 March. The balance on our ledger has been reduced accordingly.

Beatriz thanked Bluefin Health (in absentia) and thanked Aiden for applying the credit so promptly.

5.3 Invoice BH-6620

The remaining Bluefin item was invoice BH-6620, dated 3 March, for $9,874.50, for February's on-site nurse service. Aiden explained, with apologies, that the PO match had not yet cleared because the PO (PO 7795) had been raised for $9,450.00, and the invoice was $424.50 higher. He believed that the difference related to two additional overtime shifts the nurse worked during the February flu outbreak, which the plant manager had verbally authorised, but the PO had not been amended.

Beatriz said: "I'd be very happy to approve BH-6620 as soon as the PO is amended and the match clears. If the plant manager confirms the overtime in writing, I would approve it straight away — even outside the meeting." Aiden asked if she wanted him to chase the plant manager, and Beatriz said she would mention it to the plant manager herself at the Thursday operations meeting, so there was no need for Aiden to trouble himself.

The minute-taker notes for the record that BH-6620 was not approved during this meeting. It remains awaiting PO amendment. Its due date under current terms is 2 April (3 March + 30 days), so there is ample time.

Esi asked, with evident curiosity, whether the new Net 45 terms would apply to BH-6620 since it would be paid after 1 April. Wanjiru Alvarez said that, as she understood the letter, the new terms applied to invoices dated on or after 1 April, so BH-6620 (dated 3 March) would remain on Net 30. Everyone thanked Wanjiru Alvarez for clarifying.

---------------------------------------------------------------

6. (Moved) — see item 8

---------------------------------------------------------------

7. MONTH-END CLOSE — FEBRUARY RETROSPECTIVE

Beatriz asked each person to share one thing that had gone well and one thing that might have gone better during the February close, adding that she hoped nobody would feel any pressure and that "there are no wrong answers in this room."

Esi: Went well — the accruals were posted a full day earlier than in January. Might have gone better — she felt she could have communicated more clearly with the plant about outstanding goods receipts, and she apologised to anybody who had been inconvenienced by her late-night emails.

Aiden: Went well — statement reconciliations for the top ten vendors were completed before day 3. Might have gone better — he said that if he had started the Harbor Health reconciliation a week earlier, he probably would have spotted the late fee before the statement arrived. Beatriz said kindly that he should not be so hard on himself.

Wanjiru Alvarez: Went well — no vendor master changes were rejected by the approver in February. Might have gone better — she would have liked more time to review the bank-detail change requests, which she described as "the scary ones." She mentioned that, if the volume of bank-detail changes continued to grow, it might be worth considering a second reviewer, but she was not proposing it formally at this stage.

Rosa: Went well — three long-running vendor disputes were resolved. Might have gone better — she said she had perhaps been a little too polite in one dispute and conceded a $35 freight charge she probably should have contested. Everyone laughed warmly and Beatriz said that being too polite was the nicest possible flaw.

Wanjiru Tanaka: Went well — the invoice scanning backlog was cleared by 26 February. Might have gone better — she would like to learn how to post accruals herself, so that she could be more helpful next time. Beatriz thanked her and said she would be delighted to arrange that.

Beatriz summarised by thanking everyone once again.

Close timing summary (for reference):

| Close milestone | January close | February close |
|---|---|---|
| Cut-off for invoice entry | Day 2, 5:00 p.m. | Day 2, 5:00 p.m. |
| Accruals posted | Day 4 | Day 3 |
| Top-10 vendor recs done | Day 4 | Day 2 |
| AP subledger locked | Day 5 | Day 4 |
| Sign-off by AP Manager | Day 6 | Day 5 |

---------------------------------------------------------------

8. NEW INVOICE SOFTWARE ("LedgerLeaf") — PILOT FEEDBACK

(Item moved from position 6 at Esi's kind request.)

Esi reported that the IT colleague had very kindly sent over the pilot statistics during the meeting. The team has been piloting LedgerLeaf, an invoice-capture and approval-routing tool, since 3 February, running it in parallel with the existing system for invoices from twelve selected vendors (including Harbor Health, Meridian Outfitters and Bluefin Health).

Pilot statistics (3 February – 7 March):

| Measure | Existing process | LedgerLeaf pilot |
|---|---|---|
| Invoices processed | 212 | 208 |
| Average capture time per invoice | 4 min 40 s | 1 min 55 s |
| Header fields captured correctly first time | 91% | 94% |
| Line items captured correctly first time | 87% | 79% |
| Average days, receipt to approval | 6.2 | 4.8 |
| Duplicate invoices flagged automatically | 0 | 1 |

Esi noted with a smile that the one duplicate LedgerLeaf flagged was in fact a supplier who had emailed and posted the same invoice, and that — interestingly — LedgerLeaf had NOT flagged the Meridian pair from item 4, because its duplicate check compares invoice number, vendor and amount together and the invoice numbers differed. She said that if LedgerLeaf had a "fuzzy" invoice-number setting switched on, it probably would have caught MO-9031, and she understood such a setting exists but is off by default.

There was a lively and very courteous discussion about the line-item accuracy, which is worse than the existing process. Aiden felt it was a real concern for vendors like Bluefin whose invoices have many lines. Rosa asked, with apologies for being the one to raise it, whether we would be better off rolling back to the old process entirely.

Beatriz said she did not think rolling back was warranted at this stage, given the improvement in capture time and approval speed. She said: "If the line-item accuracy were to get worse over the next month, or if we found it was causing payment errors, then we would certainly consider rolling back. But let's not decide that today." Nobody objected. No decision to roll back was taken, and no rollback has been scheduled or assigned.

Instead, Beatriz observed that a good deal of the line-item trouble seemed to come from people correcting the captured lines in different ways, and she asked Aiden to please schedule a training session on LedgerLeaf's line-item correction screen for the whole team, ideally before the end of March. Aiden agreed and said he would book it and send an invitation by Friday 21 March. (Recorded as an action item — see section 10.)

Esi mentioned that several team members had written short informal reviews of LedgerLeaf for the IT colleague, and that she had included her own as Appendix B to these minutes, with apologies for its length.

Wanjiru Alvarez asked whether the fuzzy invoice-number setting could simply be switched on. Esi said she would be happy to ask IT, but that switching it on would need the IT change board's approval, and she was not sure it would be granted this quarter. She said, "If IT approved it, I think it would be wonderful," but she was not asked to raise a formal request today and nobody took an action on it. It is noted here as an idea only.

---------------------------------------------------------------

9. ANY OTHER BUSINESS

9.1 Uncashed check #20417

Wanjiru Tanaka raised, somewhat nervously and with many apologies for bringing up something so small, that check #20417 for $612.80, issued on 9 December to a small produce-crate repair business, has still not been cashed. She was unsure whether anything should be done.

Esi explained that our checks carry a "void after 90 days" legend. 9 December + 90 days = 9 March, so the check passed its stated validity on 9 March. However, Esi said the bank would often still honour it for a short time, and that the vendor had phoned in late February to say the check was in the post back to them after being misdelivered to their old unit.

There was some discussion. Beatriz said: "Should the check still not be cashed by the end of the month, then we would void it and reissue by ACH. But I'd rather give them until the 31st, since they've told us it's on its way." Wanjiru Tanaka asked whether she should prepare the void, and Beatriz kindly said there was no need to prepare anything yet; the team would revisit it at the April meeting if it was still outstanding. The check has not been voided, and no one was assigned to void it at this time.

9.2 Office plant

Rosa asked, very sweetly, whether anyone had been watering the fern in the AP bay while she was working from home. Wanjiru Tanaka confessed that she had not, and apologised profusely. Aiden said he would water it on his way out. The minute-taker notes this for completeness, although she understands it is not a formal action item.

9.3 Thank-you note

Beatriz read aloud a handwritten note that Rosa had posted to the team before her cold, which had been sitting in Beatriz's tray. Wanjiru Tanaka was asked to type it up and include it as Appendix A, so that everyone could keep a copy. Beatriz said she found it very touching.

---------------------------------------------------------------

10. ACTION ITEMS AGREED

The following action items were formally assigned at this meeting. Each owner confirmed their agreement.

| # | Action | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Write to Harbor Health politely requesting a waiver of the $200.45 late fee on the February statement | Rosa Haddad | Fri 14 March |
| A2 | Telephone Meridian Outfitters to ask whether a second shipment was made against PO 7702 (re MO-9013 / MO-9031) | Esi Castillo | This week (by Fri 14 March) |
| A3 | Update Bluefin Health payment terms in the vendor master to Net 45, effective 1 April, and attach the vendor's letter | Wanjiru Alvarez | Wed 19 March |
| A4 | Schedule and send invitations for a team training session on LedgerLeaf's line-item correction screen | Aiden Delgado | Fri 21 March |
| A5 | Correct Bluefin Health remittance address in the February minutes and recirculate | Wanjiru Tanaka | Fri 14 March |

Conditional / parked items (NOT assigned; recorded only so that the discussion is not lost):

- P1: If Esi and Aiden confirm MO-9031 is a duplicate, place it on hold and request cancellation. (Not actioned. MO-9031 is not on hold.)
- P2: If Harbor Health grants the waiver, apply the resulting credit memo. (No credit memo has been received.)
- P3: If LedgerLeaf line-item accuracy worsens, consider a rollback to the previous process. (No rollback decided or scheduled.)
- P4: If check #20417 is not cashed by 31 March, void and reissue by ACH. (Not voided; to be revisited in April.)
- P5: If the plant manager confirms the overtime in writing, approve BH-6620. (Not approved.)
- P6: If IT's change board approves, switch on LedgerLeaf's fuzzy invoice-number matching. (Idea only.)

Approval recorded during the meeting:

- HH-44718 (Harbor Health), $18,240.00 — approved by Beatriz Moreau at 9:58 a.m.; scheduled for Thursday 13 March payment run.

No other invoice was approved at this meeting.

---------------------------------------------------------------

11. CLOSE

Beatriz closed the meeting at 10:47 a.m., thanking everyone once again for their kindness, their patience with each other, and their "wonderful attention to detail." She wished Rosa a speedy recovery. Rosa thanked everyone and said it had been a pleasure, as always.

Next meeting: Tuesday 8 April, 9:30 a.m., Conference Room B. Wanjiru Tanaka has kindly volunteered to bring more coffee.

APPENDIX A — Handwritten note from Rosa Haddad, typed up by Wanjiru Tanaka

(Typist's note: I have reproduced the note as faithfully as I could, including Rosa's crossings-out, which I've shown in [square brackets]. I do apologise if I have misread any of her handwriting; she has lovely penmanship but I am not always the best at reading cursive. Anything I could not read is marked [illegible].)

---

Dear everyone,

I hope you'll forgive me for leaving a paper note rather than sending an email, but I wanted to say this properly and I always feel an email is a little cold for a thank-you.

Thank you all so much for covering my disputes queue during the week I was off in February. I came back expecting a mountain and found a molehill — and a very neatly labelled molehill at that. Esi, I know you took the two Tidewater-freight disputes [sorry — I mean the freight disputes with the haulier, not with us, obviously!] and resolved both. APPENDIX B — Informal product review of LedgerLeaf (pilot), by Esi Castillo

(Submitted to the IT colleague on 7 March and reproduced here at Beatriz's kind invitation. I apologise in advance for the length — I'm afraid I got rather carried away.)

Overall rating: 4 out of 5 leaves 🍃🍃🍃🍃 (I'm sorry, I couldn't resist)

First, I'd like to say a very sincere thank-you to the IT team and to the LedgerLeaf onboarding contact for all the care they've taken with this pilot. I know it has meant extra work on top of everyone's normal duties, and I'm truly grateful. What follows is meant entirely constructively.

What I loved

1. Capture speed. This is honestly transformative. On the old system I would spend what felt like forever keying in header fields — vendor, invoice number, date, PO, total, tax. LedgerLeaf reads them from the PDF in a few seconds and asks me to confirm. Our pilot figures show capture time down from about 4 minutes 40 seconds to about 1 minute 55 seconds per invoice. On the roughly 400 invoices a month we'd move to the tool, that's (280 s − 115 s) × 400 = 66,000 seconds, or about 18.3 hours a month. I would happily spend those hours on vendor relationships instead.

2. Approval routing. The approval routing rules are clear and the mobile approval screen is really pleasant. Beatriz told me she approved an invoice from the car park one morning, which she said she'd never have been able to do before. Approval time (receipt to approval) fell from 6.2 days to 4.8 days in the pilot.

3. The audit trail. Every change to a captured field is recorded with who changed it and when. When Aiden and I were looking at an invoice the other week, we could see exactly who had corrected the tax line, which saved an awkward round of "was it you?" emails.

4. The vendor portal. Two of our pilot vendors have started uploading invoices directly, which means no scanning at all. Wanjiru T. was very pleased about this.

What I found more difficult

1. Line-item accuracy. I'm afraid this is the big one. In the pilot, line items were captured correctly first time on only 79% of invoices, against 87% under our old manual process. On invoices with many lines (Bluefin's nurse service invoices, for instance, which list every shift), it's noticeably worse. I've had to correct lines on nearly every Bluefin invoice. If this doesn't improve, I think it could eventually cause payment errors, and I would hate that. I'm not suggesting we give up on the tool — I just think we need to understand the correction screen better. Honestly, I'm not sure we're all using it the same way.

2. Duplicate detection. The duplicate check is quite strict: vendor + invoice number + amount must all match. That catches exact duplicates beautifully (it caught one in the pilot, a supplier who emailed and posted the same invoice), but it would not catch a duplicate with a slightly different invoice number. I understand there's a "fuzzy invoice number" option. If it were switched on, I suspect it would catch transposed digits and similar slips. I'd love to know whether IT might consider it one day, but I appreciate there may be good reasons it's off.

3. Credit memos. LedgerLeaf treats credit memos as a separate document type, which is sensible, but it took me a moment to find where to apply them. When Bluefin's credit memo came in, Aiden applied it in the old system because we weren't sure the pilot covered credit memos. I'd be grateful for guidance on this.

4. Holds. You can place a hold on an invoice in LedgerLeaf, but when you do, it sends an automatic email to the vendor saying the invoice is "on hold pending review." I understand why, but the wording feels a little abrupt for vendors we have a warm relationship with. If there were a way to customise the wording, I think it would be lovely — something like "we're just double-checking a detail and will be in touch very soon." I haven't placed any holds myself during the pilot, so I can't say how vendors react.

5. Reporting. The standard reports are good, but I'd have liked an aged-payables report that matches our old layout. I've been exporting to a spreadsheet and rebuilding it, which rather eats into the time savings.

Small things (please ignore if these are too picky!)

- The date picker defaults to US format, which confused our colleague in the Nairobi office when she tested it.
- The "approve" and "reject" buttons are quite close together on mobile. Nobody has pressed the wrong one yet, as far as I know, but I'd hate for it to happen.
- The green is a very cheerful green.

Would I recommend it?

Yes, with the gentle caveats above. If I were choosing today between keeping LedgerLeaf and going back to the old process, I would keep LedgerLeaf, but I would want training on line-item correction as a priority. I think if we could all be shown the correction screen properly, the line-item figures would improve considerably, and the time savings would more than pay for the effort.

Thank you so much again for letting me take part in the pilot, and for reading this far. I really do appreciate it.

With warm regards,
Esi

APPENDIX D — Glossary (kindly requested by Wanjiru Tanaka for her own learning; shared in case it helps anyone else)

- Three-way match: comparing the purchase order, the goods receipt (or service confirmation) and the invoice, to make sure quantity and price agree before payment.
- Hold: a flag on an invoice that prevents it from being included in a payment run until the flag is removed. In our old system this is silent; in LedgerLeaf it also emails the vendor.
- Credit memo: a document from a vendor reducing the amount we owe them, for example after a return or a pricing error.
- Net 30 / Net 45: payment is due 30 / 45 days after the invoice date.
- Void: to cancel a check so it can no longer be cashed; usually followed by a reissue.
- Accrual: an estimate of an expense for goods or services received but not yet invoiced, posted so the month's accounts are complete.
- Early-payment discount: a reduction some vendors offer if we pay within a short period (e.g. 1% if paid within 10 days).

Wanjiru Tanaka thanks Beatriz, Esi and Aiden for their patience in explaining these terms to her, and apologises for asking so many questions.

APPENDIX E — Notes on the vendor-hold courtesy policy (extract, reproduced for reference at Rosa's gentle suggestion)

The following is an extract from the AP team's internal guidance, "Working Courteously with Vendors," last revised in November. It is included so that the discussion in item 4 can be read in context.

Section 4.2 — Placing invoices on hold

4.2.1 An invoice may be placed on hold by any AP Specialist with system access where there is a reasonable, documented concern about its validity, including a suspected duplicate, a price or quantity variance above tolerance, or missing supporting documentation.

4.2.2 Before placing a hold on an invoice from a vendor designated "strategic" or "preferred," the AP Specialist should, where time permits, contact the vendor to seek clarification, so that the vendor does not receive an unexpected hold notification. Meridian Outfitters, Harbor Health and Bluefin Health are all designated "preferred."

4.2.3 Where the invoice's scheduled payment date is fewer than five business days away, the AP Specialist should place the hold first and contact the vendor immediately afterwards, to avoid an erroneous payment.

4.2.4 All holds should be recorded with a reason code and reviewed at least weekly.

(Minute-taker's note: MO-9031's scheduled date of 26 March was more than five business days after the meeting on 11 March, so under 4.2.2 the team chose to contact the vendor first, as recorded in item 4. No hold was placed.)

Section 4.3 — Requesting fee waivers

4.3.1 Where a vendor has charged a late fee and the lateness was attributable to Tidewater Foods, the AP Specialist may, with the AP Manager's agreement, write to the vendor to request a waiver.

4.3.2 Requests should be courteous, acknowledge the delay, and thank the vendor for its patience.

4.3.3 Any credit received as a result must be applied only once the vendor's credit memo is received; it must not be anticipated in the ledger.

---------------------------------------------------------------

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR OUTSOURCED LABORATORY TESTING
Agreement Reference: GL-MFC-2023-014

This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of 1 February 2023 (the "Effective Date") by and between Granite Labs, a clinical diagnostic laboratory with its principal administrative office at 44 Quarry Row, Suite 300 (hereinafter "the Laboratory"), and Maplecrest Family Clinic, an outpatient primary care provider with its principal office at 910 Alder Avenue (hereinafter "the Clinic"). The Laboratory and the Clinic are each referred to herein as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties".

RECITALS

WHEREAS the Clinic provides primary care services to registered patients and requires, from time to time, the analysis of blood, urine and other specimens collected on its premises; and

WHEREAS the Laboratory holds the necessary accreditation to perform such analyses and wishes to provide those services to the Clinic under the terms set out below;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein, the Parties agree as follows.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Specimen" means any biological sample collected by Clinic staff from a patient and submitted to the Laboratory for analysis, together with its accompanying requisition form.

1.2 "Requisition" means the standard test request form, in paper or electronic format, completed by an authorised Clinic practitioner and identifying the patient, the tests requested, the date and time of collection, and the ordering practitioner.

1.3 "Routine Test" means any test listed in Schedule A under the heading "Routine Panel".

1.4 "Urgent Test" means any test marked as urgent on the Requisition by the ordering practitioner and listed in Schedule A under the heading "Urgent Eligible".

1.5 "Turnaround Time" means the period between the Laboratory's documented receipt of a Specimen and the release of a validated result to the Clinic's results inbox.

1.6 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday observed in the jurisdiction of the Clinic.

1.7 "Courier Service" means the scheduled transport of Specimens from the Clinic's collection room to the Laboratory's receiving department.

SECTION 2. SCOPE OF SERVICES

2.1 The Laboratory shall perform the tests listed in Schedule A on Specimens submitted by the Clinic in accordance with the Laboratory's published collection manual, as updated from time to time and notified to the Clinic in writing.

2.2 The Laboratory shall release results electronically to the Clinic's designated results inbox. Paper copies shall be provided only upon written request by the Clinic Practice Manager.

2.3 The Laboratory shall notify the ordering practitioner by telephone of any critical value, as defined in the Laboratory's critical value policy, within sixty (60) minutes of result validation.

2.4 The Clinic shall be responsible for correct patient identification, correct labelling of Specimens, and the completeness of each Requisition. Specimens that are unlabelled or mislabelled shall be rejected by the Laboratory and the Clinic shall be notified of the rejection by the end of the same Business Day.

SECTION 3. TURNAROUND TIMES

3.1 Routine Tests shall be reported within two (2) Business Days of receipt.

3.2 Urgent Tests shall be reported within four (4) hours of receipt where the Specimen is received between 08:00 and 16:00 on a Business Day.

3.3 Where the Laboratory anticipates that a Turnaround Time will not be met, it shall inform the Clinic Practice Manager in writing as soon as reasonably practicable, stating the cause and the expected revised reporting time.

SECTION 4. COURIER SERVICE

4.1 The Laboratory shall arrange a Courier Service collecting Specimens from the Clinic twice daily on Business Days, at approximately 11:30 and 16:30.

4.2 The cost of the scheduled Courier Service described in clause 4.1 shall be borne entirely by the Laboratory and shall not be invoiced to the Clinic.

4.3 Any additional, unscheduled collection requested by the Clinic shall be charged to the Clinic at the rate set out in Schedule B.

4.4 The Clinic shall store Specimens awaiting collection in accordance with the storage conditions specified in the collection manual. The Laboratory shall not be liable for the deterioration of Specimens stored incorrectly by the Clinic prior to collection.

SECTION 5. FEES AND PAYMENT

5.1 The Clinic shall pay the Laboratory the fees set out in Schedule B for each test performed.

5.2 The Laboratory shall invoice the Clinic monthly in arrears, itemising each test by date, patient reference number and test code.

5.3 Invoices shall be payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Disputed items shall be notified in writing within fifteen (15) days of the invoice date, and the undisputed balance shall be paid on time.

5.4 Fees shall remain fixed for the Initial Term unless amended in accordance with Section 11.

SECTION 6. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA PROTECTION

6.1 Each Party shall treat all patient information received under this Agreement as strictly confidential and shall process it only for the purposes of this Agreement.

6.2 The Laboratory shall retain Requisitions and results for the period required by applicable record-keeping regulations and shall destroy them securely thereafter.

6.3 Each Party shall notify the other within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware of any unauthorised access to patient information relating to this Agreement.

SECTION 7. QUALITY ASSURANCE

7.1 The Laboratory shall maintain its accreditation throughout the term of this Agreement and shall notify the Clinic immediately of any suspension, withdrawal or material change in accreditation status.

7.2 The Laboratory shall provide the Clinic, upon request and not more than once per calendar year, a summary of its external quality assessment results for the tests listed in Schedule A.

SECTION 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for an initial period of twenty-four (24) months (the "Initial Term").

8.2 Upon expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall not renew automatically. Any continuation beyond the Initial Term shall require a written amendment signed by both Parties.

SECTION 9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving not less than ninety (90) days' written notice to the other Party.

9.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach which, if capable of remedy, is not remedied within thirty (30) days of written notice specifying the breach.

9.3 Upon termination, the Clinic shall pay for all tests performed up to the date of termination.

SECTION 10. LIABILITY

10.1 Neither Party shall be liable for indirect or consequential loss arising under this Agreement.

10.2 The Laboratory's aggregate liability in any contract year shall not exceed the total fees paid by the Clinic in the preceding twelve (12) months.

SECTION 11. AMENDMENTS

11.1 No variation of this Agreement shall be effective unless made in writing, referencing this Agreement, and signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.

SECTION 12. GOVERNING LAW

12.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which the Clinic is located.

SCHEDULE A (summary)
Routine Panel: full blood count, basic metabolic panel, lipid profile, thyroid stimulating hormone, HbA1c, urinalysis.
Urgent Eligible: full blood count, basic metabolic panel, troponin, C-reactive protein.

SCHEDULE B (summary)
Fees per test as per attached price list dated 1 February 2023. Unscheduled courier collection: flat charge per collection as per price list.

Signed for Maplecrest Family Clinic: Practice Manager, on behalf of the partners

RIVERBEND COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTRE
APPOINTMENT BOOKING, CANCELLATION AND NON-ATTENDANCE POLICY
Policy Number: ADM-07
Version: 4.2
Approved by: Operations Committee
Policy Owner: Leila Iyer, Head of Patient Administration
Date of Approval: 9 September 2024
Next Scheduled Review: September 2026

1. PURPOSE

1.1 This policy sets out the procedures by which patients of Riverbend Community Health Centre ("the Centre") may book, amend and cancel appointments, and the administrative consequences of failing to attend a booked appointment without adequate notice.

1.2 The policy aims to ensure fair access to limited clinical time, to reduce the number of wasted appointment slots, and to provide patients with clear, consistent information about their responsibilities and the Centre's obligations.

2. SCOPE

2.1 This policy applies to all registered patients of the Centre and to all appointment types offered by the Centre, including general practitioner consultations, practice nurse appointments, physiotherapy sessions, dietetic reviews and chronic disease clinics.

2.2 This policy does not apply to walk-in minor injury services, which operate on a first-come, first-served basis and are not pre-booked.

2.3 This policy applies to all administrative staff, reception staff and clinical staff involved in booking or managing appointments.

3. DEFINITIONS

3.1 "Appointment" means a pre-booked time slot allocated to a named patient with a named clinician or service.

3.2 "Adequate notice" means notice of cancellation received by the Centre not less than twenty-four (24) hours before the scheduled start time of the appointment.

3.3 "Late cancellation" means a cancellation received less than twenty-four (24) hours before the scheduled start time.

3.4 "Non-attendance" or "no-show" means a failure to attend a booked appointment where no cancellation has been received before the scheduled start time.

3.5 "Late arrival" means arrival more than fifteen (15) minutes after the scheduled start time of an appointment of thirty (30) minutes or less.

4. BOOKING APPOINTMENTS

4.1 Patients may book appointments by telephone during reception opening hours, in person at the reception desk, or through the Centre's online patient portal.

4.2 Appointments may not be booked by email. Emails requesting appointments will receive an automated reply directing the patient to one of the booking channels listed in clause 4.1.

4.3 Routine appointments may be booked up to six (6) weeks in advance. Same-day appointments are released at 08:00 each weekday and are allocated by telephone only.

4.4 Patients booking on behalf of another person must be recorded as an authorised representative on that person's record, unless the patient is a child under the age of sixteen and the caller is a parent or legal guardian.

4.5 At the time of booking, reception staff shall confirm the patient's name, date of birth, and current contact telephone number, and shall inform the patient of the date, time, location and clinician for the appointment.

5. APPOINTMENT REMINDERS

5.1 The Centre sends an automated text message reminder to the patient's registered mobile number forty-eight (48) hours before each appointment.

5.2 Reminders are a courtesy. Failure to receive a reminder, for whatever reason, does not excuse a patient from the obligations set out in this policy.

5.3 Patients who do not wish to receive text message reminders may opt out by informing reception in writing.

6. CANCELLING OR AMENDING APPOINTMENTS

6.1 Patients who are unable to attend an appointment are asked to cancel as early as possible so that the slot can be offered to another patient.

6.2 Cancellations are accepted through the following channels:
(a) by telephone to the reception line during opening hours;
(b) through the online patient portal, at any time;
(c) by replying "CANCEL" to the automated text message reminder;
(d) in person at the reception desk.

6.3 Cancellations are not accepted by email, by social media message, or by voicemail left outside opening hours. A patient who attempts to cancel by one of these means will be treated as not having cancelled.

6.4 When a cancellation is received, staff shall record the date and time of the cancellation and the channel used in the appointment record.

6.5 Amendments to the date or time of an appointment are treated as a cancellation of the original appointment followed by a new booking.

7. NON-ATTENDANCE AND LATE CANCELLATION

7.1 The Centre records every non-attendance and every late cancellation on the patient's record.

7.2 An administrative fee of twenty-five (25.00) currency units is applied for each non-attendance at a physiotherapy or dietetic appointment. No fee is applied for non-attendance at general practitioner or practice nurse appointments.

7.3 Late cancellation of a physiotherapy or dietetic appointment incurs an administrative fee of ten (10.00) currency units.

7.4 A patient who records three (3) non-attendances within any rolling twelve (12) month period will receive a written warning letter from the Head of Patient Administration.

7.5 A patient who records a further non-attendance within six (6) months of receiving a warning letter may be required to book appointments only on the same day, by telephone, for a period of up to three (3) months. This restriction does not apply to appointments for children under sixteen, antenatal care, or urgent clinical need as determined by a clinician.

8. EXEMPTIONS AND WAIVERS

8.1 The administrative fees described in section 7 shall be waived where the patient demonstrates that the non-attendance or late cancellation resulted from:
(a) an emergency hospital admission of the patient or a dependant;
(b) the death of an immediate family member;
(c) a documented failure of the Centre's own booking systems.

8.2 Adverse weather, transport delays and work commitments do not constitute grounds for a waiver.

8.3 Requests for a waiver must be made in writing to the Head of Patient Administration within fourteen (14) days of the missed appointment.

8.4 Decisions on waiver requests shall be communicated to the patient in writing within ten (10) working days of receipt of the request.

9. LATE ARRIVALS

9.1 A patient who arrives late may be asked to rebook if the clinician is unable to see them without delaying subsequent patients.

9.2 Where a late-arriving patient is asked to rebook, the appointment is recorded as a late arrival and not as a non-attendance. No fee is applied.

10. VULNERABLE PATIENTS

10.1 Before issuing a warning letter or applying a booking restriction, staff shall review the patient's record for any flag indicating vulnerability, including learning disability, severe mental illness, safeguarding concern, or registered carer status.

10.2 Where such a flag is present, the case shall be referred to the patient's usual clinician before any action is taken under clauses 7.4 or 7.5.

11. RESPONSIBILITIES

11.1 Reception staff are responsible for recording cancellations and non-attendances accurately and promptly.

11.2 The Head of Patient Administration is responsible for issuing warning letters, deciding waiver requests, and monitoring compliance with this policy.

11.3 The Operations Committee receives a quarterly report on non-attendance rates by service.

12. COMPLAINTS

12.1 Patients who are dissatisfied with a decision made under this policy may raise a complaint through the Centre's complaints procedure, policy ADM-02.

13. MONITORING AND REVIEW

13.1 This policy shall be reviewed every two years or earlier if required by changes in legislation, service delivery, or audit findings.

13.2 Revision history:
- Version 4.0 (March 2021): introduced portal cancellation.
- Version 4.1 (June 2023): introduced text message reply cancellation; removed fax.
- Version 4.2 (September 2024): revised administrative fee amounts; clarified vulnerable patient procedure.

Related documents: ADM-02 Complaints Procedure; ADM-05 Patient Registration; CLIN-11 Safeguarding Adults and Children.

For queries about this policy, contact the Patient Administration Office during opening hours.

PARTIES

(1) Foxglove Software, a developer of healthcare administration software, with its registered office at 18 Orchard Mews ("the Licensor").

(2) Cedarfield Dental and Medical Group, operating three outpatient clinics, with its administrative headquarters at 402 Birchwood Road ("the Licensee").

Commencement Date: 1 June 2022

BACKGROUND

(A) The Licensor has developed a proprietary patient appointment scheduling platform known as "Foxglove Scheduler", comprising a web-based booking interface, an automated reminder module, a waiting-list module and a reporting dashboard.

(B) The Licensee wishes to obtain a licence to use Foxglove Scheduler at its clinics and to receive associated support services on the terms set out below.

OPERATIVE PROVISIONS

Clause 1. Interpretation

1.1 In this Agreement, "Software" means Foxglove Scheduler in object code form, including all updates and upgrades made available by the Licensor under this Agreement.

1.2 "Authorised User" means an employee or contractor of the Licensee who has been issued with individual login credentials to access the Software.

1.3 "Site" means a clinic location of the Licensee listed in Schedule 1.

1.4 "Support Hours" means 08:00 to 18:00, Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

1.5 "Service Level" means the availability and response commitments set out in Schedule 3.

1.6 "Licence Fee" means the annual fee payable by the Licensee as set out in Schedule 2.

Clause 2. Grant of Licence

2.1 Subject to payment of the Licence Fee, the Licensor grants the Licensee a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to permit Authorised Users to access and use the Software at the Sites for the purpose of managing patient appointments.

2.2 The licence permits up to forty (40) Authorised Users at any one time across all Sites.

2.3 The Licensee shall not sub-license, sell, rent or otherwise make the Software available to any third party.

2.4 The Licensee shall not attempt to reverse engineer, decompile or modify the Software except to the extent expressly permitted by applicable law.

Clause 3. Implementation

3.1 The Licensor shall configure the Software for the Licensee's appointment types, clinician rosters and opening hours within forty-five (45) days of the Commencement Date.

3.2 The Licensor shall provide two (2) days of on-site training at each Site for reception and administrative staff.

3.3 The Licensee shall provide the Licensor with an export of existing appointment data in a format agreed by the Parties, and shall be responsible for the accuracy of that data.

Clause 4. Support and Maintenance

4.1 The Licensor shall provide telephone and email support during Support Hours.

4.2 The Licensor shall respond to reported faults in accordance with the priority levels in Schedule 3.

4.3 The Licensor shall make available updates correcting defects and security vulnerabilities at no additional charge.

4.4 New modules not listed in Background paragraph (A) are not included in the Licence Fee and may be offered separately.

Clause 5. Fees

5.1 The Licensee shall pay the annual Licence Fee of 18,000.00 currency units, invoiced annually in advance on each anniversary of the Commencement Date.

5.2 Payment is due within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.

5.3 Additional Authorised Users above the limit in clause 2.2 may be added at 400.00 currency units per user per year, pro-rated.

5.4 Late payments shall bear interest at two percent (2%) per annum above the base rate from the due date until payment.

Clause 6. Data Protection

6.1 The Licensee is the controller of all patient personal data entered into the Software. The Licensor acts as processor and shall process such data only on the documented instructions of the Licensee.

6.2 Patient data shall be hosted in data centres located within the Licensee's jurisdiction.

6.3 The Licensor shall notify the Licensee without undue delay, and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours, of becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting the Licensee's data.

6.4 On termination, the Licensor shall return all patient data to the Licensee in a standard export format within thirty (30) days and shall thereafter delete all copies.

Clause 7. Service Levels

7.1 The Licensor shall use reasonable endeavours to ensure that the Software is available ninety-nine point five percent (99.5%) of the time in each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance.

7.2 Scheduled maintenance shall be carried out outside the Licensee's clinic opening hours and notified at least five (5) days in advance.

7.3 Where availability falls below the level in clause 7.1 in any month, the Licensee shall be entitled to a service credit as set out in Schedule 3.

Clause 8. Term and Termination

8.1 This Agreement shall continue for an initial term of three (3) years from the Commencement Date and shall thereafter renew automatically for successive periods of one (1) year unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the current term.

8.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach not remedied within thirty (30) days of notice.

8.3 The Licensee may terminate for convenience on one hundred and twenty (120) days' written notice, but shall not be entitled to a refund of any Licence Fee paid in advance.

Clause 9. Limitation of Liability

9.1 The Licensor's total liability in any year shall not exceed the Licence Fee paid in that year.

9.2 Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud.

Clause 10. General
